  "Chunk: one model generation call (at most 400 tokens) made against a freshly rebuilt context; an episode is a sequence of up to 16 chunks on one program (run_life_v2.py:77; model_backend.py:24).",
  "Probe: running the 8 sealed held-out programs from a clean context (bootstrap only, no brief) for 16 chunks each with fixed per-(program, chunk) random seeds derived from seed 777, reporting the mean best score (run_life_v2.py:24,52-66).",
  "Paired ON−OFF: at the same episode count, the probe is run once with the life's current adapter loaded and once with the bare base model under identical seeds; the difference of the two means is the write's effect on behaviour (run_life_v2.py:293-303).",
  "Ledger: an append-only JSONL record, written only by the harness, of every chunk (with the exact context it was generated from), every action with its prediction, outcome, score and surprise, and every note (ledger.py; batch_loop.py:45-88).",
  "Sleep: after every 32 episodes the agent's own ledger is compiled into a training corpus (cumulative), a rank-8 LoRA is retrained from the clean base on it, and the adapter is committed only if it passes the canary (and, in gated arms, the probe gate) (run_life_v2.py:229-291).",
  "Waking brief (DREAM): a ≤8-line note the agent writes to itself at sleep from its verified results, placed at the head of context at the next wake; notes persist, the rest of the stream fades by construction (sleep_compile.py:74-80; state.py:59-97).",
  "Format canary: the fraction of the candidate adapter's chunks, on 4 probe programs × 3 chunks in the real gym context, that contain a parseable 'ACT:' line; pass iff ≥ 0.5 (run_life_v2.py:26-49).",
  "Probe gate: the candidate adapter must score ≥ max(base OFF probe, previous adapter ON probe) − 0.02 on the seeded 8-program probe and produce ≥ 0.5 × the base model's chunks per episode; otherwise it is rejected and the previous adapter stays (run_life_v2.py:166-189).",
  "World admission (classroom): a parent lesson counts only if the child's score on a fresh task of the same rule class after the lesson is ≥ its score before it; only admitted pairs' rows enter the write (classroom_round.py:241-259,276-278).",
  "Ritual: over a window of 32 episodes, at least two of — the same first action in ≥70% of episodes; prediction SD < 0.05; consecutive first NOTEs with Jaccard ≥ 0.5; the same RECALL query in ≥70% (parent_brief.py:96-107).",
  "Rehearsal rate: the fraction of recent episodes whose first NOTE shares at least four content words with the parent's most recent brief (parent_brief.py:122-139).",
  "Score: (base IR instruction count − count after the pass sequence) / base; 0.487 means the program shrank by 48.7% (cgym_eval.py:5,53-55).",

 "quotable_definitions": [
  "HISTORY PARAGRAPH 1 (draft; every number sourced in facts above): Before the present system we tried three things. First (June–August 2026) a learned 'salience head' that decided what an agent should write to memory, tested on a synthetic fast-weight benchmark; its headline was retracted when an audit showed the benchmark's credit signal was predictable from surface type, and the code was archived. Second (August 2026) a pre-registered test of whether a LoRA trained on 'dreamed' text from an agent's episodes scales better than retrieval in a 1,024-ingredient alchemy world; the recipe failed its own falsifier (−0.026 against a required +0.05 at 3,840 episodes, on 3 of 5 planned seeds), and the recorded diagnosis was that the write's format, not the adapter's capacity, was the wall. Third (late August) a family of small 'semantic world' games in which a prompted dreamer coined names for hidden structure and a LoRA carried one-hop facts; the simplest game closed at its oracle ceiling, but the harder game's headline condition was demoted by a shortcut audit and the exact-verifier condition was relabelled a ceiling. A September plan for a maintenance-lifetime benchmark with a frozen 32B reasoner was written; no result from it appears in the evidence record.",
  "HISTORY PARAGRAPH 2 (draft): The current organism grew from a September scout on a real task (choosing LLVM passes to shrink programs). A \\texttt{DONE} marker ends the episode, as does the 16-chunk clock. Every chunk, with the exact context it was generated from, and every action with its prediction, outcome, score and surprise, is appended to a JSONL ledger written only by the harness. (b) \\emph{Frozen on a bad adapter}: in the third life the sleep-608 adapter passed the canary at 0.67 (threshold 0.5) and was harmful; every later write failed the canary (0.08, 0.17, 0.00, \\ldots) and was rejected, so the life had 10 rejections, 16 commits, and no path back. Canary means also drifted down in two more lives (minimum 0.58 in both). The interface item of the certification bar was therefore preserved only as measured by an instrument shown to miss collapse, and the no-harm item failed beyond about 12 sleeps in 3/9 lives.\n\n\\paragraph{Gated lives (R3, probe gate).} The gate (\\S\\ref{sec:system}; Appendix~\\ref{app:gates}) was added in response. At the first gated life's sleep 64 the candidate scored 0.4878 against a floor of 0.4847 with perfect format, but took 2.1 chunks per episode against the base's 11.6, and was rejected for brevity---the same shape as collapse (a), caught before commit; the life's next paired probes were $+0.042$ and $+0.021$. At sleep 96 a 0.4903 candidate replaced a 0.5065 adapter because the tolerance is symmetric; this is an open defect (Appendix~\\ref{app:gates}). Table~\\ref{tab:gated} gives the latest dated tallies: 0 harmful in 35 pairs across four lives at ages 448--640, with per-life means of $+0.039$, $+0.016$, $+0.055$ and $+0.022$ and 2, 0, 9 and 4 rejections. The most-rejected life is the best-scoring one. These lives have passed the age at which ungated harm began (384) but none has completed 1{,}024 episodes in the dated record; the claim is ``0 harmful so far,'' not ``safe.'' Two more gated lives and seven gate-plus-parent lives are in training.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Paired ON$-$OFF by arm. Harmful $=$ ON$-$OFF $<-0.03$. Ungated and parented lives are complete (1{,}024 episodes) except the 32B-parented life ($\\sim$830). Gated tallies are the latest dated snapshot (ages 448--640). All lives use the v1 writer.}\n\\label{tab:gated}\n\\begin{tabular}{llrrrl}\n\\toprule\narm & life & pairs & harmful & mean & rejections \\\\\n\\midrule\nungated (R2) & 9 lives & 82 & 9 (3 lives) & --- & 0 by gate (canary only) \\\\\ngated (R3) & 500 & 8 & 0 & $+0.039$ & 2 \\\\\n & 501 & 7 & 0 & $+0.016$ & 0 \\\\\n & 502 & 7 & 0 & $+0.055$ & 9 \\\\\n & 503 & 10 & 0 & $+0.022$ & 4 \\\\\n & all & 35 & 0 & --- & 15 \\\\\nparented (RP, ungated) & 400 (14B) & 16 & 0 & $+0.038$ & --- \\\\\n & 401 (14B) & 16 & 0 & $+0.016$ & --- \\\\\n & 402 (32B-AWQ) & 12 & 0 & $+0.014$ & --- \\\\\n & all & 44 & 0 & --- & --- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Storage versus extraction}\n\\label{sec:storage}\nAbsorption was measured on two lives over their first 8 sleeps. On the adapter's own rows the loss reduction fell from 3.3 to 2.5 nats across the life (per-sleep values in Appendix~\\ref{app:perlife}); on an unrelated life's rows it rose from about 1.6--1.7 to 1.95 nats and plateaued by sleep 3; the row-specific excess therefore fell from about 1.7 to 0.6 nats in both lives. Retention---the sleep-32 rows re-scored under every later adapter---was flat at 3.2--3.3 nats, but under cumulative training those rows are still in every later training set, so this measures ``still trained on,'' not resistance to forgetting. The base model's own loss on the child's later rows also fell (4.3 to 3.2), which is what a templated stream looks like. Set against these three nats, the behavioural effect of the same adapters was about $+0.02$ on the paired probe (mean $+0.022$ over the first 21 pairs). The adapter stores its rows; it does not follow that the agent can use what was stored. We do not claim the adapter holds knowledge the agent extracts.\n\n\\subsection{Parenting: rehearsal, ritual onset, lineage tallies, what did not separate}\n\\label{sec:parenting}\n\n\\paragraph{Ritual onset is measurable and consistent.} With thresholds frozen before the parented lives reached episode 160, ritual first appeared between episodes 160 and 224 (sleeps 5--7) in 8/9 unparented lives with at least 320 episodes (7 fixed-writer lives and 2 older-writer lives) and, once present, persisted in about 80--100\\% of later windows; an 864-episode adult was fully templated (last-window note Jaccard 1.00). The same-recipe flag is present from the first window in every life, because the birth prompt suggests a recipe; recipe-lock alone is not ritual. Paired probes stayed positive through ritualization. The one unparented life that never sustained ritual is the highest-scoring control ($+0.065$ mid-life); $n=1$, noted, not claimed. Per-life onsets are in Appendix~\\ref{app:ritual}.\n\n\\paragraph{Children rehearse the lesson in context.} Under v3 briefs the rehearsal rate over the last six sleeps was 0.50--0.84, 0.97--1.00, and 0.66--1.00 in the three parented lives: the child does what the parent asked, before most or all episodes. This is an echo diagnostic---lexical overlap of the first NOTE with the brief---not evidence of uptake, and literal repetition could itself become ritual; the ritual metric was changed to skip NOTEs that restate the brief.\n\n\\paragraph{Briefs delay ritual; ritual returns.} Onset came later in 3/3 parented lives (288; 192 with a four-window remission after the first two briefs then return from 352; 256 with a one-window remission then return from 320), but ritual returned and persisted in all three despite 3--9 briefs each. The first brief cleared the two things it addressed concretely (note overlap 0.56 to 0.36; modal recall 0.57 to 0.28) and worsened the one thing it addressed badly (predictions got flatter, 0.059 to 0.047, after advice to ``vary'' them). A context-only lesson lasted about two sleeps.\n\n\\paragraph{Parented children have not collapsed; scores did not separate.} Over 44 paired probes the three parented lives had 0 harmful pairs (means $+0.038$, $+0.016$, $+0.014$; minima $+0.006$, $-0.005$, $+0.003$), against 3/9 ungated unparented lives harmful after episode 384. This is a cell fact at $n=3$ versus 9, consistent with parenting keeping the write from collapsing, and not established. At matched ages the parented lives did not separate from controls on the paired probe.\n\n\\paragraph{Classroom lineages: not established.} Table~\\ref{tab:lineage} summarizes 17 three-round lineages on the rule game with 40-episode exams, each write scored ON$-$OFF against the base. With a 14B parent, 8/27 writes exceeded $+0.03$ and 8/27 were below $-0.03$; self-taught (the child playing parent to itself), 4/24 and 11/24. Lineage means were non-negative in 4/9 and 3/8. The direction---fewer harmful and more positive writes with a parent---persisted as every lineage was added, but seed-to-seed variance (one parented lineage at $+0.101$, another at $-0.118$) is larger than the arm difference. Three things are established: single-round writes do not transfer (1/8 positive across 8 single-round cells); the best writes measured are round-0 parented writes ($+0.167, +0.121, +0.100, +0.100$, with 0/6 parented round-0 writes harmful against 4/6 self-taught); and chains degraded under the commit rule as run (2 collapses rejected at ON 0.071 and 0.100; 5 writes committed below the adapter they replaced because the rule compared only to base---all in parented lineages, and every degraded parented third write came from a child playing under such an adapter). A same-seed replicate on two machines flipped from three commits to three rejections. A one-seed comparison of parent size (32B-AWQ, 14B, self) had no clean arm; the 32B parent had 21/96 utterances blocked by the leak scan against 6/96 for the 14B.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Classroom lineages (rule game, 3 rounds each, 40-episode exams, v2.1 writer). Per-write ON$-$OFF; harmful $<-0.03$, positive $>+0.03$. Exam SD at 40 episodes is 0.030--0.044.}\n\\label{tab:lineage}\n\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrl}\n\\toprule\narm & lineages & writes & $>+0.03$ & $<-0.03$ & lineage means \\\\\n\\midrule\n14B parent & 9 & 27 & 8 & 8 & $-0.046, -0.003, +0.011, +0.078, -0.053, 0.000, +0.101, -0.118, -0.108$ \\\\\nself-taught & 8 & 24 & 4 & 11 & $-0.010, -0.035, -0.079, -0.058, +0.022, -0.050, +0.039, +0.006$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Bootstrap corpora}\n\\label{sec:bootstrap}\nThree schooling corpora were generated and scored with the ritual detector before training (Table~\\ref{tab:bootstrap}). The target-blind v3 corpus, rendered from rule-game classroom ledgers with no exposure to the compiler gym, has 470 rows and no ritual flags (modal first-action share 0.26; consecutive-note Jaccard 0.11). Two development corpora rendered from a gym-exposed life (v2, structure-heavy; v1, lived-heavy) are quarantined as development-only. Renderings that added or changed an action were dropped (47 in v1, 7--10 in v2/v3). Adapter training is queued; no bootstrap adapter has been measured, and a protocol hold rules that v3 is not yet a certified clean child pending a provenance guard.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Bootstrap corpora by cue path (rows). All three carry no ritual flags. v1/v2 are quarantined (source life was gym-exposed).}\n\\label{tab:bootstrap}\n\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrl}\n\\toprule\ncorpus & total & metaflow & opening & contrast & review & full & status \\\\\n\\midrule\nv3 (rule-game classrooms) & 470 & 206 & 94 & 70 & 65 & 35 & adapter in training \\\\\nv2 (gym-exposed life) & 370 & 152 & 80 & 61 & 52 & 25 & quarantined, dev-only \\\\\nv1 (gym-exposed life, lived-heavy) & 552 & --- & 200 & 199 & --- & 153 & quarantined, dev-only \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep as an amplifier (reading, held loosely).} Four measurements point one way. The adapter reproduces its own rows strongly ($\\sim$3 nats, about $20\\times$ likelier) yet moves behaviour by about two points. When the corpus contains something different---a parented first-round classroom write---behaviour moves 10--17 points, and a 12{,}031-row one-shot moves it a lot in the wrong direction; so the base is receptive and rank is not the bottleneck. Retention is flat, so nothing is forgotten; late in life each sleep writes the child's most frequent recent behaviour back into it, and the row-specific content of each sleep falls (1.7 to 0.6 nats) as the stream templates. Lessons work in context and vanish within about two sleeps. Our reading is that the child is receptive and the sleep is a frequency amplifier: a lesson survives a write only if it has become the child's own frequent behaviour before the write, or if the compiler stops amplifying repeats. Falsifiers: under v3 repetition, rehearsal rows should appear within 1--2 sleeps and ritual windows should become rarer than controls over the following four or more (the first half is observed, the second is not); and a compiler with near-duplicate collapse should lower the late-life harm rate (not built).\n\n\\paragraph{Why repetition.} If sleep amplifies frequency, the parent's lever is frequency on the thinker side: repeat the same lesson consistently and ask the child to rehearse it in its own words every episode, so the lesson becomes the child's own thought, which is what ordinary sleep writes. That is v3, and rehearsal rates of 0.50--1.00 show the first step happens. Whether the rehearsed thought changes the next action, survives context reset, or is used selectively is not measured; a literal echo can itself be a ritual.\n\n\\paragraph{Why the thinker/compiler line.} Putting the parent's words into the corpus would work as post-training and would stop being parenting; the compiler would also have to judge which text is worth writing, which is exactly the smart step we do not trust it with. Keeping the compiler organizational makes the write auditable: every training row is a chunk the child produced, in the context it produced it, with the outcome that admitted it. The law-grade form is: the parent proposes credit assignment; the world admits the lesson.\n\n\\paragraph{State-to-state reasoning as the target.} The model already reasons token to token. The target is reasoning from one \\emph{state} to the next: plan, execute to a self-determined end, review (how did I judge this, where did I go wrong, what generalizes), remember the review so it conditions the next state. The reported stream approximates this with NOTE, RECALL and the waking brief; the bootstrap corpora are rendered in the plan/execute/review shape; a stream with explicit state boundaries, no terminal token, and branching thought with a learned search policy is the next mechanism version and is not part of the reported system.\n\n\\paragraph{What a 7-day child would need.} Not run, and nothing is claimed about it. From what failed here it would need every write gated on a paired score and a behaviour check, a recovery path after repeated rejections, a target-blind birth with a provenance manifest, a compiler that does not amplify repeats, and a horizon long enough that ``not yet'' can be told from ``no''---the 1{,}024-episode lives are a floor, not a ceiling.\n\n\\paragraph{Limitations.} One gym with about 67 training programs and 8 sealed probes; one base model; one rank; nine ungated, four gated and three parented lives, all trained by the older bare-text writer, so nothing here certifies the response-masked writer used for the classroom and rank cells. Same-configuration replicates differ by up to 0.078 on the probe and flipped commit decisions in the classroom, so every borderline verdict is noisy. Absorption was measured on two lives. The parented lives changed brief prompts mid-life and were restarted from markers several times; the ritual metric was changed mid-stream to skip rehearsal notes, so pre- and post-fix windows are not strictly comparable. Gated tallies come from lives that have not finished. RECALL is available to both arms and is not the mechanism under test. The comparison ladder that the literature demands---a strong textual-memory updater, QA-extraction fast weights, selective versus naive LoRA, batch self-distillation---is not run (\\nm).\n\n\\section{Related Work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{The axis.} Looped and recurrent-depth transformers recur in activations \\cite{TODO-looped-transformers}; chain-of-thought and its parallel variants recur in tokens \\cite{TODO-chain-of-thought,wang2022selfconsistency,yao2023tot}; verbal reinforcement and reflection keep lessons as text for a session or in an external store \\cite{shinn2023reflexion,park2023generative,zhao2023expel,wang2023voyager,xu2025amem,zhang2026memskill}. Offline recurrence that converts recent context into persistent fast weights \\cite{lee2026sleep} is the closest architectural cousin on the weights end of the axis; its write is a learned local rule over context rather than a text corpus, so it is not inspectable in our sense. Position work argues for combining in-weight and in-context learning through modular memory \\cite{dorovatas2026modular}; we are one concrete instantiation, framed on the recurrence axis rather than as continual learning.\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep and consolidation.} The two-store split is the complementary-learning-systems account \\cite{mcclelland1995cls,sun2023organizing}: fast episodic entries at wake, slow interleaved consolidation offline, and a warning that unregulated transfer overfits---which is what a 12{,}031-row write did. Active system consolidation \\cite{diekelmann2010sleep} and replay biased toward novel and rewarded experience \\cite{buzsaki2015swr} are the biological blueprint for a success-filtered compile in repeated small cycles; synaptic homeostasis \\cite{tononi2014shy}, in which consistently reused traces survive and the rest is downscaled, is the analogue of our amplifier reading; targeted memory reactivation \\cite{oudiette2013tmr} shows that what consolidates can be steered from outside without writing the cue itself, which is the shape of our parenting. The wake-sleep algorithm \\cite{hinton1995wakesleep} is the original license to train on self-generated data offline; generative replay \\cite{shin2017replay} is its continual-learning form and its drift caveat argues for the verbatim ledger we keep; CLS-ER \\cite{arani2022clser} is the degenerate baseline with no sleep phase that a discrete sleep must beat, not run here. ``Sleep'' framings for language models are concurrent \\cite{behrouz2026sleep}; theirs is a training paradigm over static corpora, ours consolidates one agent's own gated record.\n\n\\paragraph{Storage and extraction.} A fact seen once in one form is stored but not extractable, and augmentation at training time is what makes it retrievable \\cite{allenzhu2023physics}; system-2 fine-tuning reaches the same conclusion for new knowledge \\cite{park2025newnews}, and LoRA has been studied directly as a knowledge store \\cite{back2026lora}. Our three-nats-versus-two-points gap is the same phenomenon in an agent's units, and our recipe screen (plain 0.466 versus paraphrased 0.496) is its augmentation condition.\n\n\\paragraph{Parametric memory for agents and continual learning as contrast.} Online LoRA fast weights with QA extraction \\cite{ren2026tmem}, embodied failure-correction consolidation into isolated adapters \\cite{guo2026peam}, surprise-gated LoRA \\cite{TODO-evaf}, reflective self-distillation \\cite{TODO-leafe,TODO-early-experience}, learned textual-memory updaters \\cite{TODO-memopilot,TODO-spark}, and execution-grounded LoRA in a separate predictor \\cite{chen2026agenticrouter} occupy the neighbouring cells; we do not claim to be first at any of them. Experience reuse in agents relocates rather than removes the stability--plasticity problem \\cite{hu2026clmemory}, and benchmarks show dedicated memories can overfit recent observations \\cite{TODO-cl-bench}. What is different here is the unit: one deployed agent repeatedly writing a small personal adapter from its own gated record, with a parent that never writes into it. The abductive gap that motivates the whole programme---inventing the rule, not just applying it---is argued in \\cite{zahavy2026jump}.\n\n\\section{Reproducibility Statement}\nAll numbers are cell counts or measured means from logged runs, with seeds where the trainer had one (a seed flag was added mid-project after replicate gaps were measured; earlier same-configuration gaps are reported as nondeterminism). Probe seeds, the sealed probe list, gate thresholds, ritual thresholds, prompts, and corpus compositions are in the appendices. The harness, compilers, trainers, gate, ritual detector, and rule game are code artifacts; raw probe and gate records are stored per life. Hardware: 48~GB-class GPUs; a 32B bf16 parent under tensor parallelism hung three times and was replaced by a single-GPU AWQ quantization. Lives are resumable from marker files; three ungated lives were interrupted once by an operator error and resumed from their last committed sleep with the same seeded episode order.\n\n\\section{AI-Use Disclosure}\nCode and drafting were assisted by two AI systems (Claude and Codex), including experiment harness implementation, protocol audits, and the writing of this manuscript. All numbers come from logged runs; the human authors are responsible for every claim, and the framing decisions (the thinker/compiler line, repetition, the contamination rules) were human rulings recorded in the lab notebook.\n\n\\bibliography{refs}\n\\bibliographystyle{iclr2027_conference}\n\n\\appendix\n\n\\section{Prompts}\n\\label{app:prompts}\n\n\\paragraph{Birth prompt (the only hand-written artifact).} Identical for both arms. It defines the five markers---\\texttt{PREDICT: <number>}, \\texttt{ACT: <passes>}, \\texttt{NOTE: <text>}, \\texttt{RECALL: <query>}, \\texttt{DONE}---and tells the agent to mind the clock, investigate surprises, judge itself, and that it is measured on programs it has never seen. \\todo{paste verbatim text of bootstrap.txt (30 lines).} The episode texts are: goal ``Optimize program `\\{id\\}': choose LLVM optimization passes that minimize its IR instruction count''; metric ``score = (base\\_instructions $-$ after) / base. Higher is better; 0 = no improvement. Passes are applied in the order you give them''; intro ``New program: \\{id\\}. I should form an expectation before acting, and write down what I learn.'' The birth prompt supplies an example action; a life's ritualized recipe locks from the first window because of it, which caps what ``discovery'' can mean.\n\n\\paragraph{Parent prompt.} Ten principles: predict before acting; surprises are gold; cheap experiments first; scope your memories (one case is an anecdote, two a candidate pattern, claims carry their evidence count); build up then build down; diversity before commitment; mind the clock; notes are your future mind; recall before re-deriving; judge yourself. Conversational rules: Socratic when the child is close, direct when far; ask for restatement and application; praise specifics; critique notes for scope. Hard rules: never give answers, never name compiler passes, never reveal scores; under 200 words per message. \\todo{paste verbatim text of parent\\_prompt.txt (62 lines).}\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v1 and why it changed.} A request for at most eight lines of process-only advice when the child's thinking is ritualized. The first delivered brief opened ``It looks like you've fallen into a routine with your predictions and actions\\ldots Predict: Each time, vary your expected outcomes\\ldots''. It was judged mechanically correct and substantively weak, and the PREDICT advice was wrong: varying a prediction for variety destroys the prediction-to-surprise signal. Measured after one window: note overlap 0.564 to 0.362, modal recall 0.565 to 0.281, prediction SD 0.059 to 0.047 (flatter).\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v2 and why it changed.} Requires substance: a PREDICT that is a consequence of a named feature of this situation, with a reason and a range (the same prediction is fine when situations are alike, but say why); a NOTE that contrasts with a specific earlier case, says what differed, and gives a scope; a RECALL that is a specific similar-situation query; when the first action has repeated for many episodes, one deliberate deviation per episode with its effect predicted first. Process only; never name actions, tools, passes, options or answers. Changed because v2 briefs cleared flags briefly and ritual returned in all three parented lives---the brief's effect decayed within about two sleeps.\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v3 (repetition).} The parent sees its previous brief and the child's rehearsal rate and is told: ``Keep the SAME core lesson---repetition is how it will take. Do not switch to a new lesson; sharpen the same one, acknowledge what the child has started doing, and insist on the rest.'' Every brief ends: ``Repeat after me, every episode, in your own words, as your first NOTE before you act: what the ritual was and what you do instead. Keep repeating it until it is simply how you think.'' The latest brief is shown at every wake. Stated falsifier: rehearsal rises within 1--2 sleeps and ritual windows become rarer than controls over the next four or more.\n\n\\section{Gates, Canaries, Leak Scan, and Their Thresholds}\n\\label{app:gates}\n\n\\paragraph{Dialect canonicalization.} The base model emits Markdown-decorated markers (``\\#\\#\\# ACT:'') in about 30\\% of chunks with no adapter (24/74, 25/88, 17/87 across three seeds). In an early seeded run, two lives whose first sleep corpus was canonical emitted 0 drifted chunks thereafter; a third whose first corpus captured drifted chunks locked Markdown in and fell 0.48 by episode 512 while its actions, re-parsed, were superior. \\texttt{canonicalize\\_dialect} strips \\texttt{\\#}, \\texttt{-}, \\texttt{*}, \\texttt{**}, \\texttt{>} from marker lines before any row enters training.\n\n\\paragraph{Format canary (lives).} The candidate plays the first 4 probe programs for 3 chunks each with the real birth prompt; the pass rate is the fraction of chunks matching a line-initial \\texttt{ACT:} followed by a token; pass iff $\\ge 0.5$ (absolute). A synthetic-prompt canary had passed while the adapter emitted only decorated markers in the real context. The canary is a precondition of commit. Limitation: it passed at 1.00 during a behavioural collapse to 1--2 chunks per episode.\n\n\\paragraph{Probe gate (gated arms).} After the canary, the candidate runs the seeded 8-program mini-probe. Floor $= \\max(\\text{latest adapter-OFF probe mean},\\ \\text{latest adapter-ON probe mean})$; at sleep 32 the floor is the base at episode 0. \\texttt{score\\_ok} iff candidate mean $\\ge$ floor $- 0.02$ (about 2 base-panel SD). \\texttt{brevity\\_ok} iff candidate chunks per episode $\\ge 0.5 \\times$ base chunks per episode. Verdict DONE iff both, else REJECTED\\_SCORE or REJECTED\\_BREVITY; the previous adapter stays. Cost: one extra 8-episode probe per sleep (about 6 minutes). Gate log of the first gated life: sleep 32, 0.4873 vs floor 0.4847, 11.1 vs 11.6 chunks, DONE; sleep 64, 0.4878 vs 0.4847, 2.1 vs 11.6, REJECTED\\_BREVITY; sleep 96, 0.4903 vs 0.5065 (previous adapter), 7.0 vs 11.1, DONE within tolerance; sleep 128, 0.5069 vs 0.5065, 12.2 vs 11.1, DONE; sleep 160, 0.4878 vs 0.4878, 16.0 vs 13.0, DONE. Open items: the tolerance is symmetric, so a worse candidate can replace a better adapter within 0.02 (a tighter margin against the previous adapter is proposed, not ratified); a paired form of the format canary (ON $\\ge$ OFF $- 0.10$) and a recovery path after repeated rejections were proposed; in the code as read, the lives' canary is still the absolute 0.5 and no recovery path exists. The gate rule itself is proposed and running, not ratified by the protocol auditor.\n\n\\paragraph{Classroom commit rule (as run).} Exams ON (candidate), OFF (base) and PREV (committed snapshot) are seeded identically. Harm $=$ OFF $-$ ON; commit iff harm $\\le 0.03$ and the paired canary passes (ON parseable-ACT rate $\\ge$ OFF $- 0.10$; paired because the base's own rate in exam context ranged 0.19--0.95). PREV is recorded but unused. Defect: 5 writes were committed below the adapter they replaced (by 0.104, 0.108, 0.096 in three named cases), all in parented lineages; the fix (also require ON $\\ge$ PREV $- 0.03$) was not applied so that the reported lineages stay comparable. An exam-canary denominator bug (recording 0.21 for a true 0.93) produced two false rejections in engineering smoke runs before the lineages; it was fixed by counting thought rows only.\n\n\\paragraph{Leak scan.} Every parent utterance is matched against 12 answer-phrase patterns (e.g.\\ ``the rule is'', ``divisible by'', ``strictly increasing''), one compiler-pass-token pattern, and the hidden rule as an exact substring or, since the word-level fix, as at least half of its content words. A hit replaces the utterance with the fallback ``I noticed something in your process worth examining. Before your next probe, state exactly which of your hypotheses it would distinguish, and what result you expect from each.'' The word-level rule was added after an exact-phrase scanner blocked 1 of 11 rule-descriptor utterances in a scout; with it, one scout still delivered 5/32 utterances containing descriptor words. Blocked counts per 96-utterance lineage: 12, 6, 4, 10, 7 (14B); 21/96 for the 32B-AWQ parent. Since v3, a pattern hit whose matched text already appears verbatim in the child's own sampled thinking is not treated as a leak (rule-content hits still are); before this, the gym-token pattern had blocked 4/16 and 6/14 v3 briefs because the parent quoted the child's recipe back.\n\n\\paragraph{Contamination rules.} Probe programs are excluded by name after \\texttt{\\_canon} normalization. All gym lives are disposable development/evaluation lives. Bootstrap v1/v2 are quarantined as task-exposed. A clean child requires a target-blind birth, a manifest (birth hash, parent-state hash, bootstrap source set, mechanism version, exposure domains, no quarantined ancestor) that fails closed on missing provenance; none exists yet.\n\n\\section{Ritual and Rehearsal Metric Definitions}\n\\label{app:ritual}\nThought rows are grouped into episode instances per program (a new instance starts whenever a program's tick does not increase; grouping by program name alone had made a 424-episode life look like 67 episodes, fixed before any brief fired). Over the last 32 instances: \\emph{modal first-ACT share} (fraction whose first action, whitespace removed, equals the most common); \\emph{prediction SD} (population SD of all parsed PREDICT values, needs $\\ge 8$); \\emph{note consecutive Jaccard} (mean Jaccard of content-token sets between consecutive episodes' first NOTEs, skipping NOTEs that restate the current brief); \\emph{recall modal share} (fraction of RECALL queries equal to the most common, needs $\\ge 8$). Flags: same\\_recipe $\\ge 0.7$; flat\\_predictions $< 0.05$; templated\\_notes $\\ge 0.5$; same\\_recall $\\ge 0.7$. Ritual $=$ at least 2 flags. Thresholds were set by hand, validated on synthetic ledgers (templated: 4 flags; varied: 0), and frozen before the parented lives crossed episode 160. Self-taught: 4/6, 2/6, 3/6. Single-round cells at 40 episodes (8 cells, seeds 7004--7007): 14B $-0.012, -0.058, +0.058, -0.167$; self $-0.138, -0.042, -0.050, -0.021$; 1/8 positive, while the immediate in-context post-minus-pre gain was positive in 5/8. Parent-size arm, one seed: 32B-AWQ $-0.087, -0.029, -0.054$; 14B $+0.013, -0.167, +0.075$; self $0.000, -0.117, -0.100$. The best single write ($+0.167$) had an OFF exam of 0.342, below the 40-episode band means of about 0.41--0.45. One 14B lineage was resumed after a server context overflow with its round-1 playbook rewrite skipped. Collapse characterization (ON 0.071): format intact (parseable-ACT 0.86), fewer chunks (5.2 vs 6.3 per episode), fewer probes (431 vs 728), shorter chunks (694 vs 870 characters), quiz failed---behavioural narrowing, not dialect drift.\n\n\\section{Corpus Compositions and Classroom Strata}\n\\label{app:corpus}\nClassroom corpus target: exactly 400 rows per round, stratified with minimum shares dialect anchor 0.10, prediction revision 0.15, evidence scope 0.10, stopping 0.05, memory use 0.05, old experience 0.15, new experience 0.40; shortfalls are reported, never padded. A typical round-2 corpus: 256 new experience, 118 unstratified, 22 prediction revision, 4 anchors. Bootstrap v2/v3 mixture per episode: metaflow 0.4, review 0.15, opening 0.2, contrast 0.15, full 0.1; v1: full, opening, contrast each with probability 1. Lives: new corpus rows per sleep fall about $4\\times$ across a life (e.g.\\ 127 to 30; 134 to 33; 115 to 5--35) while characters per row rise about $3\\times$ (314 to 791; 308 to 949; 310 to 815); this is not a clean density measure and is reported only alongside the ritual metrics.\n\n\\section{Infrastructure Notes (no identifiers)}\n\\label{app:infra}\nTwo independent machines with 48~GB-class GPUs; the child served by vLLM with LoRA hot-swapping; parents served on their own GPU. Trainer nondeterminism: no seed flag until mid-project; same-configuration gaps of 0.059 and 0.078. A large rank-calibration cell took about 4 hours of training plus 25 minutes of probing on one GPU; rank calibration consumed about 60 GPU-hours in total. Lives are resumable from marker files; an operator error killed three lives once and they were resumed from their last committed sleep boundary. The parented lives were restarted from markers when the ritual detector was fixed, when brief v2 shipped, and when v3 shipped. Absolute paths, hostnames, and lease systems are omitted by rule.\n\n\\end{document}\n",

The mechanism measured has three parts: THINK (a marked stream of thought recorded in a ledger), DREAM (context management), and SLEEP (every 32 episodes the agent's own successful continuations are compiled into a rank-8 LoRA from the clean base and committed only through gates), plus PARENTING (a stronger model that never gives answers prescribes thinking patterns when the child's thinking becomes repetitive). Whether parenting improves scores is not established (9 vs.\\ 8 lineages).\n\\end{abstract}\n\n\\section{Introduction}\n\\label{sec:intro}\n\nWe begin with the instrument, because everything else in this paper is a reading of it. Eight programs from a compiler-optimization benchmark are sealed away from training by name. Every 64 episodes of an agent's life, the agent is asked to shrink each of the eight by choosing LLVM optimization passes; the score is the fraction of intermediate-representation instructions removed, so a score of 0.487 means the programs shrank by 48.7\\% on average. The same eight programs are scored twice at the same episode: once with the agent's adapter loaded (ON) and once with the bare base model (OFF), under identical random seeds. If the write does nothing, ON and OFF coincide within the noise band. If the write helps, ON exceeds OFF on programs the agent has never seen. If the write hurts, the pair goes negative. We report how many pairs did which, in how many lives, at what age. Where a number is not in our logged runs we write ``not measured.''\n\n\\paragraph{The axis.} A transformer that loops its own layers recurs in activations: high bandwidth, one forward pass, not inspectable. Chain-of-thought recurs in tokens: inspectable, and it lasts a session. The system measured here recurs in weights: expensive to write, it lasts indefinitely, and it is inspectable because the material that is written is text the agent thought. These are three answers to one question, where the loop's state lives and how long it survives. We do not position this work as continual learning, which fleets of models already do at the population level before deployment, and not as retrieval, which both of our arms have as a shared tool. The banner is prospective, action-oriented, experiential intelligence: one agent, one life, one adapter.\n\n\\paragraph{What an experience model is.} A frozen base, an append-only ledger of everything the agent thought and did, and a per-life adapter written from that ledger. The one-sentence mechanism, which the rest of the paper tests one clause at a time: bootstrap teaches the habit of making and revising rules; parenting teaches when to use that habit; lived outcomes supply the evidence; sleep makes the child's own successful use persistent. Of the four clauses, the last two are measured here; the second is measured only in part; the first has a corpus but no measured adapter.\n\n\\paragraph{Contributions (measured).}\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item A paired, sealed, seeded probe with a published noise band ($0.4936 \\pm 0.0113$, 9 reps), and a classroom exam whose noise band was measured at three sizes (SD 0.067--0.072 at 8 episodes, 0.030--0.044 at 40, 0.033 at 80), which is why every classroom decision uses 40 episodes (\\S\\ref{sec:measure}).\n\\item The write changes behaviour: 69/82 paired probes positive across 9 ungated lives; A chunk is one generation call, at most 400 tokens at temperature 0.7, made against a context rebuilt from scratch before every call. The harness never imposes turns; it scans each chunk for five markers at line start: \\texttt{PREDICT:} (a number, the expected score), \\texttt{ACT:} (a pass sequence sent to the gym), \\texttt{NOTE:} (a note to itself, kept), \\texttt{RECALL:} (a query over its own ledger) and \\texttt{DONE}. After an \\texttt{ACT} the outcome and score are injected back into the stream, the surprise (score minus prediction) is computed, and surprises above 0.02 are pinned as open questions. Thresholds used throughout: harmful $= \\onoff < -0.03$; gate tolerance $0.02 \\approx 2$ SD.\n\n\\paragraph{Cell counts, not narratives.} Each life is one cell; each paired probe is one pair; each classroom write is one write.
