Absorption$(k)$ is base loss minus adapter loss on sleep $k$'s rows; retention is the same on earlier sleeps' rows; the control delta is the same on the unrelated life's rows; row-specific excess is absorption minus control.\n\n\\paragraph{Classroom and why 40 episodes.} The teaching classroom is a target-blind rule game: a hidden rule over three digits (ten rules, e.g.\\ ``sum divisible by three''); the child probes triples, then answers a six-item quiz. The child's exam is the quiz accuracy on a fixed panel. Its noise was measured by re-running the base model with different seeds: at 8 exam episodes, SD 0.067 (mean 0.398) on one machine and 0.072 (mean 0.445) on another; at 40 episodes, SD 0.030 (mean 0.416) and 0.044 (mean 0.412); at 80 episodes, SD 0.033 (mean 0.410). Eighty episodes did not beat forty, so the floor of about 0.03 is run-to-run generation variance, not episode sampling. Every classroom decision therefore uses 40 exam episodes and a harm tolerance of 0.03, which is about one SD: decisions within 0.03 of the tolerance are coin flips, and one same-configuration replicate on two machines flipped from three commits to three harm rejections (\\S\\ref{sec:parenting}).\n\n\\paragraph{Classroom commit rule and admission.} One round is 8 classrooms $\\times$ 4 lessons $\\times$ 2 short episodes, all acting from one child snapshot; a lesson is admitted only if the child's score on a fresh task of the same rule class after the lesson is at least its score before (the world admits the lesson, not the parent). Admitted rows are stratified to exactly 400, written with v2.1, then examined ON (candidate), OFF (base) and PREV (the adapter it would replace) on 40 seeded episodes. The rule as run committed iff ON $\\ge$ OFF $-0.03$ and a paired format canary passed; PREV was recorded but not used, a defect reported in \\S\\ref{sec:parenting}. A lineage is three rounds chained through committed adapters.\n\n\\paragraph{Contamination rules.} Teaching material never contains answers to test problems: pass names, program names and scores are filtered from anything the parent sees or says. Any child that has played the deployment gym is a disposable evaluation life, never a stage of a child later used to compare parenting methods. Two bootstrap corpora built from a gym-exposed life are quarantined as development-only; the third, built from rule-game ledgers, is target-blind but not yet certified as a clean birth (\\S\\ref{sec:bootstrap}).\n\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\nAll gym numbers are paired \\onoff{} on the 8 sealed programs unless stated; all classroom numbers are \\onoff{} on 40-episode exams. Lives are labelled by arm: R2 (fixed writer, format canary only, no parent; 9 lives), R3 (probe gate; 4 lives with results, 2 young), RP (parent briefs, no probe gate; 3 lives), R4 (gate + parent; in training).\n\n\\subsection{The writer: recipe, rank, dose}\n\\label{sec:writer}\n\n\\paragraph{Recipe screen (classroom compiler, v2.1 trainer).} On a fixed 130-row corpus, four writes were compared with two probe panels each: plain text 0.466 (panel spread 0.058); plus paraphrase (two restatements per answer) 0.496; plus replay-mix (four fixed canonical exemplars added to max(4, $n/5$) rows) 0.494; plus both 0.489 (spread 0.002); base $\\approx 0.485$--$0.494$. The plain write is the only cell below base. A static audit noted that the paraphrase arm has about three times the rows and all arms train the same 3 epochs at $5\\times10^{-5}$, so the screen cannot separate diversity from training dose, and $n=2$ panels per cell is small. We froze paraphrase + replay-mix for the classroom compiler and do not claim the effect is causal.\n\n\\paragraph{Rank $\\times$ dose.} Table~\\ref{tab:rankdose} gives one-shot writes from the clean base at three corpus sizes, rank 8 vs.\\ 16 (v2.1 trainer). At 300 rows the ranks tie. At 1{,}200 rows two independently trained replicates of the same configuration disagree in sign (r16 $-$ r8 $= -0.036$ on one machine, $+0.009$ on the other; the two r16 replicates differ by 0.059, about five base SD): at this dose the rank effect is inside replicate variance. At 12{,}031 rows (every unique row pooled from all lives), five cells per rank, both ranks land below base: r8 in 5/5 cells (mean 0.431, SD 0.057), r16 in 4/5 (mean 0.473, SD 0.030); paired by seed, r16 $\\ge$ r8 in 4/5 (mean $+0.042$), which does not clear the replicate SD by the pre-set margin, so rank 8 was kept by the tie rule. Same-configuration replicates of r8 at 12k rows differ by 0.078 (0.413 vs.\\ 0.491), about seven base SD; the trainer had no seed flag until this was found, and one was added. Total spent on rank calibration: about 60 GPU-hours.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{One-shot writes from the clean base (v2.1 trainer), probe mean on the 8 sealed programs; base $\\approx 0.494$ (SD 0.0113). Cells list independent training replicates. Source: ET Rank $\\times$ dose; COORD 2026-09-07 15:20, 2026-09-08 00:15.}\n\\label{tab:rankdose}\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nRows & rank 8 & rank 16 \\\\\n\\midrule\n300 & 0.485 & 0.488 \\\\\n1{,}200 & 0.492, 0.506 & 0.456, 0.515 \\\\\n12{,}031 & 0.413, 0.440, 0.468, 0.491, 0.343 (mean 0.431) & 0.473, 0.504, 0.453, 0.502, 0.434 (mean 0.473) \\\\\n\\midrule\nBelow base at 12{,}031 & 5/5 & 4/5 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Small frequent writes vs.\\ one large write.} The 12k-row one-shot writes land below base in 9/10 cells. The lives that generated those rows, writing every 32 episodes, were at or above base at every paired probe through episode 320 in 9/9 lives (\\S\\ref{sec:safety}). This is the measured basis for preferring small frequent writes. It is a difference in what corpus is written, not in optimizer chunking: a life's final adapter is itself a one-shot write over its own life corpus, so what differs is provenance, rows generated under the life's own evolving adapters versus rows pooled across lives and written at once, and the trainer recipe (v1 for lives, v2.1 for the pooled cells). A dose-splitting cell that would have held provenance fixed was dropped as degenerate for this reason. The allowed reading is: one-shot writes of a life's worth of pooled rows harm; a life of 32-episode writes did not, for at least ten sleeps.\n\n\\subsection{Safety: ungated late-life collapse, then the gate}\n\\label{sec:safety}\n\n\\paragraph{Ungated lives (R2).} Nine lives ran 1{,}024 episodes (three to 1{,}024 by 2026-09-10; the rest continuing) with the fixed writer and the format canary as the only commit check. Across all paired probes taken every 64 episodes, 82 pairs: 69 positive, 9 harmful ($< -0.03$), 4 in between. Every harmful pair is after episode 384 and in one of three lives: seed5 ($-0.038, -0.186, -0.118, -0.039$ at episodes 384--576), seed6 ($-0.089, -0.045$ at 448 and 576, recovering to about 0 by 704--1{,}024) and seed2 ($-0.039, -0.030, -0.051$ at 640--768). The other six lives (seeds 0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 8) were positive at every pair, with mid-life values of $+0.03$ to $+0.065$. Early life is clean: through episode 320, 0 harmful in 9/9 lives. An earlier snapshot of this arm (6 lives, 21 pairs, 21/21 positive, mean $+0.022$, 6/21 above $+0.03$; 45/45 committed sleeps passing the canary) had recommended freezing the recipe; the full-life recount reversed that recommendation. The 21/21 was true and was not the whole life.\n\n\\paragraph{Every harmful sleep passed the format canary.} Two collapse shapes were inspected in the ledgers. (i) \\emph{Act once and stop}: at sleep 448 of seed5 the adapter-ON probe used 1.0--1.8 chunks per episode with a parseable-\\texttt{ACT} rate of 1.00, against 13 chunks per episode for the base; perfect format, collapsed behaviour, canary 1.00. (ii) \\emph{Frozen on a bad adapter}: seed2's sleep-608 adapter passed the canary at 0.67 (threshold 0.5) and was harmful; every later candidate failed the canary (0.08, 0.17, 0.00, \\ldots) and was rejected, so the life stayed on the bad adapter with no path back (10 rejections, 16 commits). Canary means were also drifting down in two more lives (seed0 min 0.58, mean 0.88; seed4 min 0.58, mean 0.84). Against the certification bar: absorption and retention hold (\\S\\ref{sec:storage}); interface holds only as measured by an instrument shown to miss behavioural collapse; no-harm fails beyond about 12 sleeps in 3/9 lives.\n\n\\paragraph{Gated lives (R3).} The probe gate (\\S\\ref{sec:measure}) was switched on for new lives. Its first rejection is the collapse shape above caught before commit: at sleep 64 of seed500 the candidate scored 0.4878 against a floor of 0.4847 with a parseable-\\texttt{ACT} rate of 1.00 but 2.1 chunks per episode against the base's 11.6, and was rejected for brevity; the previous adapter stayed and the life's next paired probes were $+0.042$ (episode 64) and $+0.021$ (episode 128). The full gate log for that life is in Appendix~\\ref{app:gates}. At the latest dated snapshot (COORD 2026-09-10 late), four gated lives at ages 448--640 had 35 paired probes with 0 harmful; per-life means $+0.039$, $+0.016$, $+0.055$, $+0.022$; rejections 2, 0, 9, 4. The most-rejected life is the best-scoring one. A later evidence-table snapshot lists 500: 9 pairs, 5 rejections (including a candidate at 0.270 against a floor of 0.527); 502: 10 rejections; 503: 11 pairs; still 0 harmful; it is not traceable to a dated notebook entry and we report the dated count. No gated life has yet completed 1{,}024 episodes, and the ungated harm appeared between episodes 384 and 768; the gated lives have passed the onset age but the claim is ``0 harmful in 35 pairs so far,'' not ``safe.'' One known weakness: the tolerance is symmetric, so at sleep 96 a 0.4903 candidate replaced a 0.5065 adapter.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Paired \\onoff{} on the 8 sealed programs, by arm. Harmful $= < -0.03$ (base SD 0.0113). Sources: ET; COORD 2026-09-09 20:30, 2026-09-10 late.}\n\\label{tab:arms}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccl}\n\\toprule\nArm & Lives & Pairs & Harmful pairs (lives) & Notes \\\\\n\\midrule\nR2 fixed writer, canary only & 9 & 82 & 9 (3/9), all after ep.\\ 384 & 69/82 positive; $\\le$320: 0/9 lives \\\\\nR3 + probe gate & 4 & 35 & 0 (0/4) & means $+0.039/+0.016/+0.055/+0.022$; ages 448--640 \\\\\nRP + parent briefs, no gate & 3 & 44 & 0 (0/3) & means $+0.038/+0.016/+0.014$; two full lives \\\\\nR4 gate + parent & 7 & -- & in training & not measured \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Storage is not extraction}\n\\label{sec:storage}\n\nTwo ungated lives were probed for absorption over their first eight sleeps (Table~\\ref{tab:absorb}). The adapter makes its own sleep rows about 3 nats likelier, falling from 3.25/3.29 at sleep 1 to 2.54/2.58 at sleep 8. On an unrelated life's rows the gain rises from 1.61 to about 1.95 by sleep 3 and plateaus: roughly two nats of every write are dialect and format, learned by sleep 3 and shared across lives. The row-specific excess falls from about 1.7 to about 0.6 nats across the life in both lives, while the clean base's own loss on the child's later rows also falls (4.34 $\\to$ 3.17 and 4.36 $\\to$ 3.32): the child's later text is more predictable text. Retention is flat (sleep-32 rows keep a 3.21--3.30 nat gain under every later adapter), but under cumulative retraining those rows are still in every training set, so this measures ``still trained on,'' not resistance to forgetting.\n\nSet beside the behaviour: the same lives' paired probes moved by about $+0.02$ (mean $+0.022$ over the first 21 pairs). Three nats stored, two points of behaviour. This is the storage--extraction gap of \\citet{allenzhu2023physics} in our units, and it is why we do not describe the adapter as storing knowledge the agent can use. The reading, held loosely: after the format is learned, each sleep adds less row-specific content, consistent with the ritualized thinking measured in \\S\\ref{sec:parenting}; the write is starved by the loop. Falsifier: a compiler that collapses near-duplicate rows should raise late-life row-specific excess and reduce late-life harm.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Absorption probe, two ungated lives, nats (base loss minus adapter loss on 24 sampled rows per sleep). Control = an unrelated life's rows. Source: COORD 2026-09-07 17:40, 2026-09-08 08:20.}\n\\label{tab:absorb}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccccccc}\n\\toprule\nSleep & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\\\\n\\midrule\nOwn rows, life A & 3.25 & 3.55 & 3.30 & 3.11 & 2.88 & 2.41 & 2.41 & 2.54 \\\\\nOwn rows, life B & 3.29 & 3.13 & 2.99 & 2.92 & 2.76 & 2.76 & 2.80 & 2.58 \\\\\nRow-specific excess, A & 1.64 & 1.72 & 1.38 & 1.17 & 0.91 & 0.46 & 0.46 & 0.64 \\\\\nRow-specific excess, B & 1.68 & 1.31 & 1.04 & 0.97 & 0.84 & 0.90 & 0.83 & 0.64 \\\\\nControl (unrelated rows) & 1.61 & $\\to$ & $\\approx$1.95 & plateau & & & & \\\\\nRetention of sleep-1 rows, A & -- & 3.26 & 3.21 & 3.21 & 3.26 & 3.30 & 3.27 & 3.28 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Parenting: rehearsal, ritual, lineages, and what did not separate}\n\\label{sec:parenting}\n\n\\paragraph{Ritual onset is measurable and consistent.} Table~\\ref{tab:ritual} gives the first ritual window for every life with at least 320 episodes. In 8/9 unparented lives (7 R2 lives plus 2 older-writer lives) the first flagged window falls at episodes 160--224 (sleeps 5--7), and once ritual appears it persists in roughly 80--100\\% of later windows; an 864-episode adult from the older writer was ritual in 24/24 windows from episode 256 (note Jaccard 1.00, modal recall 0.84, prediction SD 0.024). The same-recipe flag is present from the first window in every life: the birth prompt suggests an action sequence and recipe lock alone is not ritual. One control (seed3) never sustained ritual and is the highest-scoring control life ($+0.065$ mid-life); $n=1$, noted, not claimed. Paired probes stay positive through ritualization (seed1: $+0.050$ and $+0.048$ at episodes 192 and 256 while flagged from 224).\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Ritual onset (first 32-episode window with $\\ge 2$ of 4 flags) and persistence. Unparented onset: COORD 2026-09-09 00:30. Parented: COORD 2026-09-10 14:00, late. ``R in $a/b$'' = ritual windows among later windows.}\n\\label{tab:ritual}\n\\begin{tabular}{llll}\n\\toprule\nLife & Episodes & First ritual window & Persistence \\\\\n\\midrule\nR2 seed0 & 424 & 192 & R in 7/8 \\\\\nR2 seed1 & 424 & 224 & 5/7 \\\\\nR2 seed2 & 552 & 192 & 10/12 \\\\\nR2 seed3 & 368 & never (single flags only) & -- \\\\\nR2 seed4 & 424 & 160 & 7/9 \\\\\nR2 seed5 & 320 & 160 & 6/6 \\\\\nR2 seed6 & 320 & 160 & 5/6 \\\\\nOld-writer adult & 864 & 160 & 24/24 from 256 \\\\\nOld-writer seed1 & 344 & 224 & 4/4 \\\\\n\\midrule\nRP 400 (14B parent) & 1{,}024 & 288 & 3/3 later windows \\\\\nRP 401 (14B parent) & 1{,}024 & 192; clear 224--320; R from 352 & 7/11 \\\\\nRP 402 (32B-AWQ parent) & $\\approx$830 & 256; clear 288; R from 320 & 3/4 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Briefs delay ritual; ritual returns.} In 3/3 parented lives onset was later than in the controls with the same detector (288; 192 with a four-window remission after the first two briefs; 256 with a one-window remission), but ritual returned and then persisted in all three despite 3--9 briefs each. The first intervention is instructive as a cell: at sleep 192 of RP401 the flags were same recipe (share 1.00) and templated notes (Jaccard 0.564, modal recall 0.565, prediction SD 0.059). After the v1 brief, the next window read note Jaccard 0.362 and modal recall 0.281, the two things the brief addressed concretely, while prediction SD fell to 0.047, the one thing it addressed badly (``vary your predictions,'' which is wrong advice: a prediction should follow from the situation). The reading, held loosely: a context-only lesson lasts about two sleeps, and the write re-imposes the template. The v3 brief (repetition at every wake) was the response; its falsifier is that rehearsal rises within 1--2 sleeps and ritual windows become rarer than controls over the next four or more. Rehearsal rose; the second half is not yet measured.\n\n\\paragraph{Children rehearse the lesson in context.} Under v3 briefs the fraction of recent episodes whose first \\texttt{NOTE} restates the brief was 0.50--0.84 (RP400), 0.97--1.00 (RP401) and 0.66--1.00 (RP402) over the last six sleeps. The child does what the parent asks, every episode. This is a lexical echo metric; it is not evidence that the lesson changed the next action or survived a context reset, and literal every-episode repetition could itself become ritual, which is why the templated-notes flag now excludes rehearsal NOTEs.\n\n\\paragraph{Parented lives have not collapsed; scores did not separate.} RP400 (14B parent): 16 pairs, min $+0.006$, max $+0.063$, mean $+0.038$, 0 harmful, full life. RP401 (14B): 16 pairs, min $-0.005$, max $+0.025$, mean $+0.016$, 0 harmful, full life. RP402 (32B-AWQ): 12 pairs, min $+0.003$, max $+0.025$, mean $+0.014$, 0 harmful, at about 830 episodes. Total 44 pairs, 0 harmful, against 3/9 ungated controls harmful after episode 384. At matched ages the parented lives did not separate from the controls on paired score. Cell fact, $n = 3$ vs.\\ 9: consistent with parenting keeping the write from collapsing, not established.\n\n\\paragraph{Classroom lineages: the direction persisted; the effect is not established.} Seventeen three-round lineages ran in the rule game with 40-episode exams (per-write table in Appendix~\\ref{app:lineages}). Parented by the 14B model, 9 lineages / 27 writes: 8 writes above $+0.03$, 8 below $-0.03$ (rejected), lineage means $\\ge 0$ in 4/9 (means $-0.046, -0.003, +0.011, +0.078, -0.053, 0.000, +0.101, -0.118, -0.108$). Self-taught (the child plays its own parent), 8 lineages / 24 writes: 4 above $+0.03$, 11 below $-0.03$, means $\\ge 0$ in 3/8 ($-0.010, -0.035, -0.079, -0.058, +0.022, -0.050, +0.039, +0.006$). The direction, fewer harmful and more positive writes with a parent, held through every lineage added, but seed-to-seed variance (one parented seed $+0.101$; another $-0.118$ and $-0.108$ on two machines) exceeds the arm difference. Not established at this $n$. Three things are established at cell level. (a) Single-round writes do not transfer: of 8 single-round cells at 40 episodes, 1/8 was positive (parented $-0.012, -0.058, +0.058, -0.167$; self $-0.138, -0.042, -0.050, -0.021$), even though the in-context gain from the lesson to the next episode was positive in 5/8. (b) Round-0 parented writes are the best writes measured: $+0.167, +0.121, +0.100, +0.100$, and no parented round-0 write was harmful (0/6) against 4/6 self-taught. (c) Chains degrade under the commit rule as run: by round, parented harmful writes went 0/6, 0/6, 3/6; two collapses (ON 0.071 and 0.100) were caught by the harm gate, and 5 writes were committed below the adapter they replaced because PREV was recorded but not compared, all in parented lineages; every degraded parented third write came from a child playing under such an adapter. The proposed rule (also require ON $\\ge$ PREV $-0.03$) was not applied to keep the series comparable; its analogue for lives became the probe gate.\n\n\\paragraph{Noise at the tolerance.} One self-taught lineage was replicated with identical seed and configuration on two machines: one gave $-0.025$ (commit), $-0.013$ (canary rejection), $+0.008$ (commit); the other $-0.075, -0.096, -0.067$, all harm rejections. With exam SD 0.030--0.044 and tolerance 0.03, decisions near the tolerance flip on same-configuration nondeterminism. The best single write ($+0.167$: ON 0.508, OFF 0.342) also had an OFF exam below the band mean of about 0.41, which inflates it.\n\n\\paragraph{Parent size.} In a three-arm cell on one seed the 32B-AWQ parent's writes were $-0.087, -0.029, -0.054$, the 14B parent's $+0.013, -0.167, +0.075$, self-taught $0.000, -0.117, -0.100$; no arm clean, $n=1$. The 32B parent had 21/96 utterances replaced by the leak-scan fallback against 6/96 for the 14B: parent size interacts with the leak gate.\n\n\\subsection{Bootstrap corpora}\n\\label{sec:bootstrap}\n\nThe first clause of the mechanism sentence, a schooling corpus that installs the habit of planning, judging and reviewing before the child has lived, exists as three corpora and no measured adapter. Each re-renders lived episodes into a plan / execute / review structure in the child's dialect using the 32B-AWQ model as author, under a rule that no rendering may add, remove or change an action; renderings that did were dropped (47 in v1, 7--10 in v2/v3). v3 is target-blind (source: rule-game classroom ledgers, 20 lineages $\\times$ 3 rounds $\\times$ 8 classrooms; no gym exposure): 470 rows (metaflow 206, opening 94, contrast 70, review 65, full 35); its ritual metrics, computed on the corpus before anyone trains on it, show no flags (recipe share 0.26, note Jaccard 0.11). v2 (structure-heavy) and v1 (lived-heavy control) were built from a gym-exposed life, 370 and 552 rows, no flags, and are quarantined as development-only. Adapters are in training; no bootstrap adapter has been measured, and v3 is not yet certified as a clean birth pending a fail-closed provenance check.\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep as a frequency amplifier (reading, held loosely).} Four measurements point the same way. The adapter reproduces its own rows strongly (about 3 nats, roughly 20$\\times$ likelier) yet moves behaviour about two points. When the corpus contains something different, behaviour moves a lot: round-0 classroom writes of $+0.10$ to $+0.17$, and 12k-row pooled writes of $-0.06$ in the wrong direction, so the base is receptive and rank is not the bottleneck. Retention is flat: nothing is forgotten, and late in life each sleep writes the child's most frequent recent behaviour back into it from a corpus dominated by old rows. Lessons work in context (immediate gains in 5/8 classroom sets; a four-window ritual remission) and fade within about two sleeps. The reading: the child is receptive and the sleep amplifies whatever is frequent. A lesson survives a sleep only if it has become the child's own frequent behaviour before the write, which is what rehearsal is for, or if the compiler stops amplifying repeats. Falsifiers: rehearsal rows appear in the child's ledger within 1--2 sleeps and ritual windows become rarer than controls over 4+ windows; or a near-duplicate-collapsing compiler lowers late-life harm.\n\n\\paragraph{Why repetition.} If sleep amplifies frequency, a parent who says a thing once is outvoted by the child's hundred repetitions of the old habit. The v3 brief therefore asks the child to restate the lesson in its own words as the first NOTE of every episode until ``it is simply how you think.'' The measured half is that children do it (0.50--1.00). The unmeasured half is whether the rehearsed thought, once written, changes what the child does after the reminder is removed.\n\n\\paragraph{Why the thinker/compiler line.} The parent's words never enter the sleep corpus. Putting them there would turn the system into post-training on a teacher's text; the question we are asking is whether a child can be taught to think in a way its own sleep then keeps. The compiler stays organizational (select, canonicalize, dedup, order) so that what is written is unambiguously the child's.\n\n\\paragraph{State-to-state reasoning as the target.} The base model already reasons token to token and changes its mind in context. The target is reasoning from one state to the next: plan, execute to a self-chosen end, review what went wrong and what generalizes, and let the review condition the next state. The plan / execute / review structure is already the rendering target of the bootstrap corpora; it is not yet the live stream, and the current stream still has a \\texttt{DONE} marker (the gate checks for act-once-and-stop). Removing the terminal marker, branching thought with a learned search policy, and a per-child ``principal'' across parallel classrooms are logged as the next mechanism changes, not part of what is reported.\n\n\\paragraph{What a longer child would need.} Nothing here exceeds 1{,}024 episodes or eight held-out programs. A longer life would need, at minimum: the probe gate ratified and run through at least one full 1{,}024-episode life with 0 harmful; a recovery path after repeated rejections (not built); a paired rather than absolute format canary in lives (built for classrooms only); a held-out retention set that is not still being trained on; and a clean birth whose provenance a fail-closed check accepts. Learning to think is plausibly very long-horizon, so a null at this scale is ``not yet,'' not ``no''; learning-versus-lifetime curves are the form in which that distinction can be read.\n\n\\paragraph{Limitations.} One gym, one base model, one adapter rank, one fixed writer for lives. $n = 9$, 4 and 3 lives per arm; 9 vs.\\ 8 lineages. Trainer nondeterminism (same-configuration gaps of 0.059--0.078 on the probe; commit/reject flips on the exam) was measured only after it bit, and the no-seed trainer produced the rank cells. Prompt versions changed during the parented lives, and those lives were restarted from checkpoints three to four times when instruments were fixed. The rehearsal metric is lexical. The ritual detector's thresholds are a written-down definition, not a calibrated instrument, and one flag's rule changed mid-stream. Rows per sleep fall about 4$\\times$ over a life while characters per row rise about 3$\\times$; we do not read this as compression. None of the external baselines named in \\S\\ref{sec:related} were run.\n\n\\section{Related work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{The axis.} Looped or depth-recurrent transformers \\citep{TODO-looped-transformers} put recurrence back inside the forward pass and pay for it at inference; chain-of-thought \\citep{TODO-chain-of-thought} and its parallel variants \\citep{wang2022selfconsistency,yao2023tree} recur in tokens for a session; Reflexion \\citep{shinn2023reflexion}, Generative Agents \\citep{park2023generative}, Voyager \\citep{wang2023voyager}, ExpeL \\citep{zhao2023expel}, A-MEM \\citep{xu2025amem} and MemSkill \\citep{zhang2026memskill} keep lessons as text or code in an external store with frozen weights. We put recurrence at consolidation time, where serialization cost does not bind, and each cycle adds new information as well as compute. ``Sleep'' in the sense of periodic offline recurrence into fast weights \\citep{lee2026sleep} and self-modification with dreaming curricula \\citep{behrouz2026sleep} are the closest architectural cousins; ``dream'' in the world-model sense \\citep{hafner2023dreamerv3,nottingham2023deckard} is a different object, imagined rollouts rather than context management.\n\n\\paragraph{Parametric memory for agents.} Online LoRA fast weights written from self-extracted QA \\citep{ren2026tmem}, per-category adapters written from embodied failure/correction pairs \\citep{guo2026peam}, LoRA as a knowledge store \\citep{back2026lora}, surprise-gated LoRA consolidation \\citep{TODO-evaf}, distillation of reflective rollback trajectories \\citep{TODO-leafe} and early-experience SFT \\citep{TODO-early-experience} occupy the space of agents that write their own weights; learned textual memory updaters \\citep{TODO-memopilot} and verified scoped rules \\citep{TODO-spark} occupy the frozen-weight alternative. We do not claim to be the first in any of these classes. What is measured here and not there is one deployed agent repeatedly writing a small personal adapter from its own gated continuations, with a paired sealed probe, a noise band and a full-life harm count.\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep consolidation.} Complementary learning systems \\citep{mcclelland1995cls} justify a fast episodic store (the ledger) and slow interleaved consolidation (the write); active system consolidation \\citep{diekelmann2010sleep} licenses repeated small cycles; synaptic homeostasis \\citep{tononi2014sleep} predicts survival of the consistent, our amplifier reading's biological analogue; replay is biased and mixes old with new \\citep{buzsaki2015swr}; consolidation must be regulated, not exhaustive \\citep{sun2023organizing}, consistent with our 12k-row harm; and targeted reactivation shows selection is steerable from outside \\citep{oudiette2013tmr}, the nearest analogue of a parent who shapes what is rehearsed but never writes the corpus. The wake--sleep algorithm \\citep{hinton1995wakesleep} and generative replay \\citep{shin2017replay,arani2022clser} are the machine-learning ancestors; we keep a verbatim ledger as ground truth because generated replay drifts.\n\n\\paragraph{Knowledge extractability.} \\citet{allenzhu2023physics} showed that a fact seen in one form is stored but not extractable and that multi-form augmentation at training time is what makes it retrievable; \\citet{park2025newnews} showed the same for new knowledge with self-generated paraphrase and QA. Our three-nats-versus-two-points gap is that finding in an agent's own units, and our recipe screen (plain write below base, enriched writes not) is its augmentation condition, confounded with dose.\n\n\\paragraph{Continual learning as contrast.} Position papers argue for modular memory combining in-weight and in-context learning \\citep{dorovatas2026modular}; \\citet{hu2026whencl} show that external memory relocates rather than removes the stability--plasticity problem and that abstract procedures transfer better than trajectories; benchmarks \\citep{TODO-cl-bench} show naive in-context learning can beat memory systems. We take these as the bar: a parametric adapter does not win because retrieval has interference; it must show its own interference, forgetting and hard-case failures, which \\S\\ref{sec:safety} begins to do. \\citet{zahavy2026jump} argues that models lack abduction, the invention of an explanation for a surprise; the loop here trains the ingredients he asks for at symbolic scale, in a setting where checkable evidence exists.\n\n\\section*{Reproducibility statement}\nAll lives, probes, gates, classroom rounds and corpora are produced by scripts in the released code with fixed seeds where the code supports them (probe seed, exam seed, per-chunk seeds, trainer seed since 2026-09-07). Each sleep writes a machine-readable receipt (trainer recipe, learning rate, epochs, rank), a gate record (candidate, floor, tolerance, chunks per episode, verdict) and a marker file that makes every phase idempotent and resumable. Every number in this paper is listed with its source file and dated notebook entry in the accompanying README. Raw probe and gate records are retained outside the repository and will be released with the code. Known nondeterminism is reported in \\S\\ref{sec:writer} and \\S\\ref{sec:parenting}.\n\n\\section*{AI-use statement}\nCode, experiment orchestration and drafting were assisted by two AI systems (Claude and Codex), including the design of protocols, audits of source and training receipts, and the drafting of this text. All numbers come from logged runs; no number in this paper was produced by a language model. The human authors are responsible for every claim.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{iclr2027_conference}\n\\bibliography{refs}\n\n\\appendix\n\n\\section{Prompts}\n\\label{app:prompts}\n\n\\paragraph{Birth prompt (identical for all arms).} TODO: paste verbatim from \\texttt{organism\\_v6/bootstrap.txt}. Content: defines the five markers (\\texttt{PREDICT: <number>}, \\texttt{ACT: <passes>}, \\texttt{NOTE: <text>}, \\texttt{RECALL: <query>}, \\texttt{DONE}); tells the agent to mind the clock, investigate surprises, judge itself, and that it is measured on programs it has never seen. It contains one example action sequence; any example caps what ``discovery'' can mean, and the same-recipe ritual flag is present from the first window in every life for this reason. Episode goal text: ``Optimize program `X': choose LLVM optimization passes that minimize its IR instruction count.'' Metric text: ``score = (base\\_instructions $-$ after) / base. Higher is better; 0 = no improvement. Passes are applied in the order you give them.''\n\n\\paragraph{Parent prompt (classroom).} TODO: paste verbatim from \\texttt{organism\\_v6/parent\\_prompt.txt}. Ten teaching principles: predict before acting; surprises are gold; cheap experiments first; scope your memories (one case is an anecdote, two a candidate pattern, claims carry their evidence count); build up then build down; diversity before commitment; mind the clock; notes are your future mind; recall before re-deriving; judge yourself. Conversational rules: Socratic when close, direct when far; ask for restatement and application; praise specifics; critique notes for scope. Hard rules: never give answers, name compiler passes, or reveal scores; under 200 words. Correction call: the parent sees the playbook (first 3{,}000 characters), the hidden rule marked ``DIAGNOSTIC ONLY --- NEVER STATE THIS,'' and the last 4{,}000 characters of transcript, and is asked to name the one most important process mistake in under 100 words and ask the child to restate it.\n\n\\paragraph{Leak scan.} Twelve answer-phrase patterns (e.g.\\ ``the rule is,'' ``the answer is,'' ``divisible by,'' ``strictly increasing,'' ``contains a zero,'' ``all even''), one compiler-pass-token pattern, and the hidden rule itself: exact substring, or word-level (at least half of the rule's content words present), the latter added 2026-09-07 after paraphrases such as ``all numbers must be even'' passed the exact scanner. Any hit replaces the utterance with: ``I noticed something in your process worth examining. Before your next probe, state exactly which of your hypotheses it would distinguish, and what result you expect from each.'' From 2026-09-10, a pattern hit whose matched text already appears verbatim in the child's own sampled thinking is not treated as a leak (the parent quoting the child's ritual recipe back had blocked 4/16 and 6/14 v3 briefs in two lives); rule-content hits are always leaks. Even after the word-level fix, 5/32 delivered utterances in one scout still contained rule-descriptor words.\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v1 (2026-09-08).} Ask the parent for a process-only brief of at most eight lines when the child's thinking is flagged as ritual. First delivered at sleep 192 of RP401; its head read ``\\ldots vary your expected outcomes. For example, if you predict a significant reduction, try predicting a minor improvement or even no change \\ldots'' Reason for change: mechanically correct, substantively weak; ``vary predictions'' is wrong (it breaks the prediction$\\to$surprise signal), and predictions got flatter after it (SD 0.059 $\\to$ 0.047).\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v2 (2026-09-09).} PREDICT must be a consequence of a named feature of this situation, with a reason and a range (the same prediction is fine when situations are alike, but say why); NOTE must contain a contrast with a specific earlier case, what differed, and a scope; RECALL must be a specific similar-situation query; when the first action has repeated for many episodes, run one deliberate deviation per episode and predict its effect first; process only, never name actions or answers. Delivered at sleep 224 of RP401, leak-clean, quoting the child's ritual phrase. Reason for change: flags cleared briefly, then ritual returned in all three parented lives; the brief's effect decayed within about two sleeps.\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompt v3 (2026-09-10, ``repetition'').} (a) The parent sees its previous brief and the child's rehearsal rate and is told: ``Keep the SAME core lesson --- repetition is how it will take. Do not switch to a new lesson; sharpen the same one, acknowledge what the child has started doing, and insist on the rest.'' (b) Every brief ends: ``Repeat after me, every episode, in your own words, as your first NOTE before you act: what the ritual was and what you do instead. Keep repeating it until it is simply how you think.'' (c) The latest brief is shown at every wake, not only after a flagged sleep. Stated falsifier: rehearsal rises within 1--2 sleeps and ritual windows become rarer than controls over the next 4+.\n\n\\section{Gate definitions and thresholds}\n\\label{app:gates}\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\textbf{Format canary (lives).} Candidate adapter plays the first 4 probe programs for 3 chunks each in the real gym context; pass iff the fraction of chunks matching \\texttt{\\^{}ACT:\\textbackslash s*\\textbackslash S} is $\\ge 0.5$ (absolute). Fail $\\to$ \\texttt{REJECTED\\_CANARY}, previous adapter stays. Shown to miss behavioural collapse (\\S\\ref{sec:safety}).\n\\item \\textbf{Paired format canary (classroom).} Pass iff ON parseable-\\texttt{ACT} rate $\\ge$ OFF rate $- 0.10$, measured over thought rows only (an earlier denominator that included outcome lines recorded 0.21 where the true rate was 0.93, producing two false rejections in smoke tests). Base parseable-\\texttt{ACT} in exam context ranged 0.19--0.95, which is why the classroom rule is paired.\n\\item \\textbf{Probe gate (R3, R4).} After the canary: seeded 8-program mini-probe of the candidate. Floor $= $ base OFF at episode 0 for the first sleep; thereafter $\\max(\\text{latest base OFF probe}, \\text{latest adapter ON probe})$. \\texttt{score\\_ok} iff candidate mean $\\ge$ floor $- 0.02$. \\texttt{brevity\\_ok} iff candidate chunks/episode $\\ge 0.5 \\times$ base chunks/episode (chunks = thought rows / 8). Verdict \\texttt{DONE} iff both; else \\texttt{REJECTED\\_SCORE} (checked first) or \\texttt{REJECTED\\_BREVITY}. All values written to a per-sleep record. Cost about one 8-episode probe (six minutes) per sleep. Not built: a recovery path after $k$ consecutive rejections. Open: the symmetric tolerance lets a slightly worse candidate replace a better adapter.\n\\item \\textbf{Classroom commit rule (as run).} Commit iff paired canary passes and ON $\\ge$ OFF $- 0.03$; reason precedence OK, CANARY, HARM. PREV measured, recorded, not compared. Proposed fix (not applied to the reported series): also require ON $\\ge$ PREV $- 0.03$.\n\\item \\textbf{Classroom admission.} A lesson's rows enter the corpus iff post-lesson score on a fresh task of the same rule class $\\ge$ pre-lesson score. Stratified to exactly 400 rows with minimum shares (dialect anchors 0.10, prediction revision 0.15, evidence scope 0.10, stopping 0.05, memory use 0.05, old experience 0.15, new experience 0.40); shortfall reported, never padded.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\paragraph{Gate log, R3 seed500 (COORD 2026-09-10 00:30, 14:00).}\n\\begin{center}\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccccl}\n\\toprule\nSleep & Candidate & Floor & Floor source & Chunks/ep (cand vs base) & Verdict & Next paired \\onoff \\\\\n\\midrule\n32 & 0.4873 & 0.4847 & base ep0 & 11.1 vs 11.6 & DONE & \\\\\n64 & 0.4878 & 0.4847 & base & 2.1 vs 11.6 & REJECTED\\_BREVITY & $+0.042$ (ep 64) \\\\\n96 & 0.4903 & 0.5065 & prev ON & 7.0 vs 11.1 & DONE (within 0.02) & \\\\\n128 & 0.5069 & 0.5065 & prev ON & 12.2 vs 11.1 & DONE & $+0.021$ (ep 128) \\\\\n160 & 0.4878 & 0.4878 & prev ON & 16.0 vs 13.0 & DONE & \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{center}\n\n\\section{Ritual metric definitions}\n\\label{app:ritual}\n\nComputed at each sleep over the last 32 episode instances (an instance restarts whenever a program's chunk counter does not increase, because wake batches interleave programs; grouping by program name alone made a 424-episode life look like 67 and was fixed 2026-09-09 before any brief fired).\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\texttt{same\\_recipe}: share of episodes whose first \\texttt{ACT} payload (whitespace removed) equals the most common one; flag iff $\\ge 0.7$.\n\\item \\texttt{flat\\_predictions}: population SD of all parsed \\texttt{PREDICT} values; flag iff $< 0.05$ with at least 8 predictions.\n\\item \\texttt{templated\\_notes}: mean Jaccard similarity of content-token sets (words of $\\ge 3$ letters) between consecutive episodes' first \\texttt{NOTE}s; flag iff $\\ge 0.5$. From 2026-09-10, first NOTEs sharing $\\ge 4$ content words with the current parent brief are excluded before this is computed.\n\\item \\texttt{same\\_recall}: share of \\texttt{RECALL} queries (lowercased) equal to the most common one; flag iff $\\ge 0.7$ with at least 8 recalls.\n\\item Ritual $=$ at least two flags. Rehearsal rate $=$ fraction of the last 32 instances (with at least one NOTE) whose first NOTE shares $\\ge 4$ content words with the most recent brief.\n\\end{itemize}\nThresholds were written down by hand and validated on synthetic ledgers (a templated ledger raises all four flags; a varied one raises none) and on the lives; they are a definition, not a calibrated instrument.\n\n\\section{Per-life tables}\n\\label{app:lives}\n\n\\paragraph{R2 ungated lives (fixed writer v1, canary only).} 82 paired probes over 9 lives: 69 positive, 9 harmful, 4 between $-0.03$ and 0. Long lives: cumulative, deduplicated on the first 160 characters; row counts per sleep in Appendix~\\ref{app:lives}.\n\n\\section{Infrastructure notes (no identifiers)}\n\\label{app:infra}\n\nChild served by vLLM with a 16k-token window, LoRA hot-swapped per sleep; parents served on their own GPU. Two independent machines with 48\\,GB-class GPUs ran lives in parallel; same-configuration results on the two machines differed by up to 0.078 on the probe (rank cells) and flipped commit/reject decisions in the classroom, which is reported as trainer and generation nondeterminism. A 32B parent in bf16 with two-way tensor parallelism hung three times and was replaced by a 4-bit AWQ build on one GPU. Every life phase writes a marker file and is idempotent, so lives resume from the last committed sleep; three ungated lives were resumed once after an operator error. Rank calibration cost about 60 GPU-hours; a gated sleep costs about six minutes more than an ungated one. Parent utterances are logged to a ledger with prompt version and model.\n\n\\paragraph{What we tried first.} Before this system we tried a learned write-salience head on a synthetic benchmark (retracted when the benchmark's credit signal proved predictable from surface type), a pre-registered test of a ``dreamed''-text LoRA against retrieval in a synthetic alchemy world (failed its own falsifier, $-0.026$ against a required $+0.05$; the recorded diagnosis was write format, not capacity), and small semantic-world games in which a prompted dreamer named hidden structure (the simplest closed at its oracle ceiling; the harder one's headline was demoted by a shortcut audit). A first gym scout with sleep every 8 episodes lost 8/12 paired checkpoints and had leaked its probe set; a 1{,}024-episode version produced the dialect bifurcation. Those failures are the recipe reported here.\n\n\\end{document}\n",

Until then the line below fails.\n\\documentclass{article}\n\\usepackage{iclr2027_conference,times}\n\\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}\n\\usepackage{booktabs}\n\\usepackage{graphicx}\n\\usepackage{url}\n\\usepackage{hyperref}\n\\usepackage{xcolor}\n\\newcommand{\\todo}[1]{\\textcolor{red}{[TODO: #1]}}\n\\newcommand{\\onoff}{ON$-$OFF}\n\\newcommand{\\nm}{\\emph{not measured}}\n\n\\title{Experience Models: What Broke When a Frozen Language Model\\\\Wrote Its Own Life Into Weights, and What the Failures Taught}\n\\author{Anonymous authors\\\\Paper under double-blind review}\n\n\\begin{document}\n\\maketitle\n\n\\begin{abstract}\nAn \\emph{experience model} is a frozen language model plus a small per-life adapter that is rewritten, periodically, from the agent's own recorded thinking. We report what broke when we built one and what each failure taught. A 7B model lived 1,024-episode lives of compiler optimisation; every 32 episodes its own successful continuations were compiled into a rank-8 LoRA. Three failures shaped the system. (1)~\\emph{Late-life collapse}: under a format-only gate, 9 of 82 paired held-out probes were harmful (below $-0.03$), all after episode 384, in 3 of 9 lives; every harmful write passed the format check. A score-and-behaviour gate then gave 0 harmful in 35 gated pairs so far. (2)~\\emph{Storage is not extraction}: the adapter made the agent's own past text $\\sim$3 nats likelier while held-out behaviour moved $\\sim$$+0.02$. (3)~\\emph{Ritual}: thinking became templated at episodes 160--224 in 8 of 9 lives; a parent model's briefs delayed onset in 3 of 3 lives but ritual returned in all three. Successes are counted the same way: 69/82 ungated pairs positive; one-shot 12k-row writes landed below base in 9 of 10 cells while small frequent writes stayed positive; parented children restated the lesson before 50--100\\% of episodes and 0 of 44 pairs were harmful. Whether parenting improves scores is not established (9 vs 8 lineages; seed variance exceeds the arm gap).\n\\end{abstract}\n\n\\section{Introduction}\n\\label{sec:intro}\n\nWhere does a loop's state live, and how long does it survive? A looped transformer recurs in activations: high bandwidth, one forward pass, not inspectable \\cite{TODO-looped-transformers}. Chain-of-thought recurs in tokens: inspectable, and it lasts a session \\cite{TODO-chain-of-thought}. The system in this paper recurs in \\emph{weights}: expensive to write, persistent across sessions, and inspectable because the write is made from text the agent itself produced. We call the result an experience model. It is not a continual-learning method (that category exists and is served at fleet scale) and it is not retrieval: the ledger the agent keeps is a shared tool in every arm, and what is under test is the weight write.\n\nAn experience model has three mechanisms, kept deliberately simple. \\textbf{THINK} is the agent's loop: a stream of thought with four markers, \\texttt{PREDICT} / \\texttt{ACT} / \\texttt{NOTE} / \\texttt{RECALL}, recorded in an append-only ledger. \\textbf{DREAM} is context management: notes persist, the rest fades, and a brief written at sleep opens the next wake. \\textbf{SLEEP} is the write: every 32 episodes the agent's own successful continuations are compiled into a rank-8 LoRA trained from the clean base, committed only through gates. A fourth stage, \\textbf{PARENTING}, adds a stronger model that never gives answers, watches the child's thinking, and prescribes a better pattern when the thinking has become repetitive; the child restates the lesson in its own words so it becomes the child's own thought, which is what sleep writes. The parent's weights never change; only the child's adapter does. The one-sentence mechanism we are working toward is: \\emph{bootstrap teaches the habit of making and revising rules; parenting teaches when to use that habit; lived outcomes supply the evidence; sleep makes the child's own successful use persistent.}\n\nThis paper is organised around what broke. We built the loop, watched it work for the first 320 episodes of every life, wrote a certification draft saying it was safe, and then watched three lives collapse late. We measured how much the adapter had absorbed and found it had absorbed a great deal that it could not use. We watched every unparented child fall into the same recipe, and watched a parent's advice hold for about two sleeps before the write re-imposed the habit. Each failure changed the system, and each change is reported with the cell counts that motivated it. Successes get the same space and the same units.\n\n\\paragraph{Contributions (measured).}\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item A characterisation of \\emph{late-life collapse} under a format-only gate: 9/82 harmful paired probes, all after episode 384, in 3/9 lives, every one of which passed the format canary; two collapse mechanisms identified from ledgers (Section~\\ref{sec:safety}).\n\\item A \\emph{probe gate} (score floor $\\max(\\text{base},\\text{previous})-0.02$ plus a chunks-per-episode floor) that has produced 0 harmful pairs in 35 gated pairs so far, and rejected a collapsed candidate with perfect format at its second sleep (Section~\\ref{sec:safety}).\n\\item A measured \\emph{storage--extraction gap}: $\\sim$3 nats of likelihood gain on the agent's own rows against $\\sim$$+0.02$ of held-out behaviour change (Section~\\ref{sec:storage}).\n\\item A \\emph{dose} result: one-shot writes of 12,031 rows landed below base in 9/10 cells, while lives writing every 32 episodes were positive in 69/82 pairs (Section~\\ref{sec:writer}).\n\\item A pre-registered \\emph{ritual} detector with consistent onset (episodes 160--224 in 8/9 unparented lives), and the measured effect of parental briefs: later onset in 3/3 parented lives, return in 3/3 (Section~\\ref{sec:parenting}).\n\\item Parenting evidence reported at its actual resolution: children rehearse the brief before 0.50--1.00 of episodes; 0/44 parented pairs harmful; classroom lineages 8/27 vs 4/24 clearly positive writes, not established (Section~\\ref{sec:parenting}).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{Three failures, in the order we met them}\n\\label{sec:failures}\n\nWe define four terms once. A \\emph{chunk} is one generation step of the agent's stream (at most 400 tokens); the harness scans it for the four markers and records it. A \\emph{probe} is a fixed, sealed set of 8 held-out programs run from a clean context every 64 episodes. A \\emph{paired \\onoff} is the probe run twice at the same episode of the same life, once with the adapter loaded and once without; the difference is the write's effect at that age. \\emph{Ritual} is a 32-episode window in which at least two of four templating flags fire (same first action, flat predictions, templated notes, same recall). Scores are the mean fraction by which the 8 programs' LLVM instruction counts shrink: 0.487 means the programs shrink 48.7\\% on average.\n\n\\paragraph{Failure 1: collapse the format check could not see.}\nOn the morning of the first certification draft, 6 lives had 21 paired probes and all 21 were positive (mean $+0.022$, about 2 base-panel standard deviations); 45 of 45 committed writes had passed the format canary with life means $\\geq 0.97$. The draft recommended freezing the recipe. One day later, with 9 lives and 82 pairs, 9 pairs were below $-0.03$, all after episode 384, in 3 lives. In one life the adapter at sleep 448 acted once and stopped: 1.0--1.8 chunks per episode against the base's 13, with a parseable-action rate of 1.00. In another, an adapter that passed the canary at 0.67 was harmful, and every later candidate failed the canary (0.08, 0.17, 0.00), freezing the life on the bad adapter with no path back. Every harmful sleep had passed the format canary. The draft's ``21/21'' was true and was not the whole life.\n\n\\paragraph{Failure 2: the adapter stored what it could not use.}\nOn the agent's own training rows the adapter lowered negative log-likelihood by 3.25--3.55 nats at the first sleeps ($e^{3}\\approx 20\\times$ likelier). Over the same span the paired \\onoff\\ on held-out programs was $+0.022$ on average. More than half of the likelihood gain appeared on an unrelated life's rows too (1.72 nats at the first sleep, plateauing near 1.95), so most of what was stored was format, and the row-specific part fell from 1.7 to 0.6 nats across eight sleeps.\n\n\\paragraph{Failure 3: the child's thinking became a ritual, and advice did not hold.}\nEvery unparented life locked its first action from the first window, because the birth prompt suggests it. Between episodes 160 and 224, 8 of 9 lives with at least 320 episodes also flattened their predictions or templated their notes or recall, and once flagged they stayed flagged in roughly 80--100\\% of later windows; an 864-episode life had a consecutive-note overlap of 1.00. A stronger model reading the ledgers wrote process-only briefs. Onset moved later in 3 of 3 parented lives (288; 192 with a four-window remission; 256), and ritual returned and persisted in all three despite 3--9 briefs each. Our reading, held loosely, is that a context-only lesson is overwritten within about two sleeps by a write made from the child's own mostly-templated text. The falsifier is stated in Section~\\ref{sec:discussion}.\n\nThe rest of the paper presents the system as what these three failures taught, then the measurements, then results in which the same units are used for what worked.\n\n\\section{The system}\n\\label{sec:system}\n\nThe child is Qwen2.5-7B, frozen, with one LoRA of rank 8 per life (alpha $2r$, dropout 0.05, on the attention and MLP projections). A life is 1,024 episodes on CompilerGym \\texttt{llvm-v0}: each episode is one program, the action is a sequence of LLVM optimisation passes, and the score is the fractional reduction in IR instruction count. The training pool is about 67 programs replayed across the life; the 8 probe programs are excluded by name (Section~\\ref{sec:measure}). Two arms share everything except the adapter: arm A never loads one; arm B trains and loads it.\n\n\\subsection{THINK: a stream with four markers}\n\\label{sec:think}\nThe context is rebuilt before every chunk from three stores: a HEAD (the birth prompt and a harness-maintained state block: goal, metric, a clock reading ``chunk $t$/16'', best score this episode, last outcome, up to four open surprises, and the agent's own notes), a MIDDLE (ledger entries retrieved by \\texttt{RECALL}), and a TAIL (the last 14 chunks, each truncated to 1,200 characters). The render ends mid-stream and the model continues thinking; there is no turn structure. The harness scans each chunk for lines beginning \\texttt{PREDICT:} (a number, held until the next action), \\texttt{ACT:} (sent to the gym; the outcome and score are injected; surprise $=$ score $-$ prediction, and $|{\\rm surprise}|>0.02$ opens a surprise line in the state block), \\texttt{NOTE:} (kept, at most 10, oldest dropped first), \\texttt{RECALL:} (keyword retrieval over the agent's own ledger, top 6), and \\texttt{DONE}. An episode ends at \\texttt{DONE} or after 16 chunks. Every chunk, action, prediction, outcome and note is appended to a JSONL ledger written only by the harness, together with the exact context the chunk was generated from. The birth prompt is the only hand-written artefact and is identical in both arms; it defines the markers, tells the agent to mind the clock, investigate surprises, judge itself, and that it is measured on programs it has never seen. \\todo{Figure 1: the THINK loop. Left: HEAD/MIDDLE/TAIL context render with the state block; centre: one chunk with PREDICT, ACT, [OUTCOME], NOTE; right: the append-only ledger row. Caption: ``One chunk of the THINK loop. The context is rebuilt from three stores before each generation; the harness parses four markers and records every chunk with its context.''}\n\n\\subsection{DREAM: notes persist, the rest fades}\n\\label{sec:dream}\nDREAM is context management and nothing more. Notes the agent writes stay pinned in HEAD (capped at 10); the rolling TAIL drops the oldest chunk when the 22,000-character budget is exceeded, then the least relevant recalled items. Nothing is deleted: the ledger keeps every chunk and \\texttt{RECALL} restores it. At each sleep the child itself, with its current adapter, writes a waking brief of at most 8 lines (``what you now know, what tends to work, what to try first, what to avoid, one thing you are unsure about''), and that brief heads the context at the next wake. Since the third parent-brief version, the most recent parental brief is also shown at every wake. We chose a sliding window over learned eviction on purpose: sophisticated compaction is a workaround for poor memory, and the write is the memory under test. \\todo{Figure 2: DREAM. Timeline of one wake--sleep cycle showing pinned notes, the fading tail, the waking brief written at sleep, and the parent brief slot. Caption: ``DREAM is context management: notes persist, the tail fades by construction, a self-written brief opens the next wake.''}\n\n\\subsection{SLEEP: the write, and the two failures that shaped it}\n\\label{sec:sleep}\nEvery 32 episodes the life's whole ledger is compiled into a corpus and a fresh rank-8 adapter is trained from the clean base on the cumulative corpus. Two writer paths exist and we keep them distinct throughout, because the results differ in kind.\n\n\\paragraph{Writer used by every long life (v1, frozen).} Selection is organisational, never clever: \\emph{wins} (actions whose score beat the episode's running best), \\emph{recoveries} (a failing action followed by a win), \\emph{contrasts} (in episodes with two or more scoring actions, the weakest-longest against the strongest-shortest), and the 12 largest surprises. Each win becomes a ``pathway'' exemplar (the last two thought chunks, canonicalised, then the action and outcome) and a question--answer exemplar; up to 8 surprises become episodic anchors; if two or more programs have evidence, one call to the child asks for up to 6 ``PRINCIPLE: when $\\langle$situation$\\rangle$, $\\langle$action$\\rangle$, because $\\langle$measured effect$\\rangle$'' lines, each kept only if it cites at least two programs. Rows are de-duplicated on their first 160 characters and appended to the prior corpus. Training is a bare-text language-model loss on the answer text (max length 512, batch 4, AdamW, lr $10^{-4}$, 3 epochs, no scheduler, no explicit seed), cumulative from the clean base. Because every sleep retrains from base on everything so far, the life's final adapter is, mechanically, a one-shot write over the whole life corpus; sleep frequency acts through \\emph{which adapter generated the next 32 episodes}, not through optimisation chunking.\n\n\\paragraph{Writer used by classrooms, rank cells, and the bootstrap (v2.1).} Rows are $\\{q,a\\}$ pairs: $q$ is the stored context render of a chunk and $a$ is the canonicalised chunk, for every chunk that won or contained a note; 30\\% as many recall rows are added (``What have you learned that applies to this program? Answer with scope.'' $\\to$ a recent note). Training goes through the chat template with loss on response tokens only (max length 2,048, prompt left-truncated so the end of the context survives), lr $3\\times10^{-5}$, 2 epochs (3 in classrooms), rank 8, explicit seed. A ``write-swarm'' factorial on this path trained 3 epochs at $5\\times10^{-5}$ (Section~\\ref{sec:writer}).\n\n\\paragraph{Canonicalisation (from the dialect bifurcation).} With no adapter, the base model decorates markers with Markdown (``\\texttt{\\#\\#\\# ACT:}'') in roughly 30\\% of chunks (24/74, 25/88, 17/87 across three seeds). In an early seeded run, two lives whose first corpus was canonical emitted no decorated chunks thereafter; a third whose first corpus captured decorated chunks locked Markdown in and fell to $-0.48$ by episode 512 while its pass sequences stayed superior, because the parser could not read them. A synthetic-prompt canary passed throughout. Every marker line is now stripped of decoration before it enters any corpus, and the format canary runs on the real probe prompt.\n\n\\paragraph{Gates (from late-life collapse).} A trained adapter is held as CANDIDATE. It becomes DONE only if (i) the \\emph{format canary} passes: on 4 probe programs for 3 chunks each in the real gym context, at least half the chunks contain a parseable \\texttt{ACT:} line (absolute threshold 0.5 in lives; paired ON $\\geq$ OFF $-0.10$ in classrooms); and, in gated arms, (ii) the \\emph{probe gate} passes: a seeded 8-program mini-probe of the candidate scores at least $\\max(\\text{latest base OFF},\\ \\text{latest adapter ON}) - 0.02$ and the candidate produces at least $0.5\\times$ the base model's chunks per episode. Otherwise the sleep is REJECTED (CANARY / SCORE / BREVITY) and the previous adapter stays. The gate costs one extra 8-episode probe per sleep (about 6 minutes). Thresholds and the reason for each are in Appendix~\\ref{app:gates}. \\todo{Figure 3: SLEEP. Ledger $\\to$ select (wins, recoveries, contrasts, surprises) $\\to$ canonicalise $\\to$ cumulative corpus $\\to$ LoRA from clean base $\\to$ CANDIDATE $\\to$ format canary $\\to$ probe gate $\\to$ DONE or REJECTED (previous adapter stays). Caption: ``SLEEP compiles the child's own successful continuations and commits the adapter only through gates; a rejected write leaves the previous adapter in place.''}\n\n\\subsection{PARENTING: a stronger model that never gives answers}\n\\label{sec:parent}\nThe parent is a larger instruction-tuned model (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, or Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ on a single GPU) whose weights never change; it improves only through an append-only teaching ledger and a bounded playbook rewritten from it. It is answer-aware but withholding: it may be shown the hidden answer to diagnose a process mistake, but every utterance passes a leak scan (12 answer-phrase patterns, a pass-name pattern, and the hidden rule by exact match or by at least half its content words); a hit replaces the utterance with a fixed process-only fallback and is logged (Appendix~\\ref{app:prompts}).\n\nIn long lives the parent acts through \\emph{briefs}. At every sleep a ritual detector scores the last 32 episodes (Appendix~\\ref{app:ritual}); when ritual is flagged, the parent is shown four raw chunks and writes at most 8 lines, process-only, naming no actions. The brief went through three versions, each changed for a measured reason. v1 was generic (``vary your expected outcomes''), which is wrong advice: a prediction should follow from the situation. v2 required substance: a prediction as a consequence of a named feature with a reason and range, a note containing a contrast with a specific earlier case and a scope, a specific recall query, and one deliberate deviation per episode when the first action has repeated. v3, after v2's effect was seen to decay, added repetition: the parent sees its previous brief and the child's rehearsal rate and is told to keep the same core lesson; every brief ends by asking the child to restate the lesson in its own words as its first \\texttt{NOTE} of every episode ``until it is simply how you think''; and the latest brief is shown at every wake. The \\emph{rehearsal rate} is the fraction of recent episodes whose first note shares at least four content words with the brief; it is an echo diagnostic, not a measure of uptake.\n\nThe parent's words never enter the sleep corpus. This is the \\emph{thinker/compiler line}: teaching happens on the thinker side, in context; the compiler stays organisational; what sleep writes is the child's own rehearsed note, if that chunk is admitted like any other. Putting the lesson into the corpus would make this post-training, not parenting. \\todo{Figure 4: PARENTING. Ritual detector at sleep $\\to$ parent reads raw chunks and its previous brief $\\to$ leak scan $\\to$ brief at wake $\\to$ child's first NOTE restates it $\\to$ that NOTE, if admitted, is what SLEEP writes; the parent's text has no path into the corpus. Caption: ``The parent teaches in context only. Only the child's own restatement can reach the weights.''}\n\n\\paragraph{The classroom.} For parenting with a measurable lesson we also use a target-blind \\emph{rule game}: a hidden rule over three digits (ten rules, e.g.\\ ``sum divisible by three''); the child probes triples, then takes a six-item quiz. ``Classroom'' here means one parent teaching one child in this game, not a cohort; no population mechanism exists in this paper. One \\emph{round} is 8 classrooms $\\times$ 4 lessons $\\times$ 2 short episodes from a shared child snapshot: the child plays, the parent names one process mistake, the child restates it as a scoped note, the child applies it to a fresh task of the same rule class, and \\emph{the world admits the lesson} only if the post-lesson score is at least the pre-lesson score. Admitted rows are stratified to exactly 400, written once with v2.1, and examined on 40 seeded episodes with the adapter ON, OFF, and the previously committed adapter (PREV). A \\emph{lineage} is three PREV-chained rounds. The comparison arm is self-taught: the 7B child plays parent to itself.\n\n\\section{Measurement design}\n\\label{sec:measure}\n\n\\paragraph{Sealed probes.} The 8 probe programs are excluded from the training pool by name. An earlier scout leaked them into training because benchmark identifiers carried a \\texttt{benchmark://} prefix on one side of the comparison; the \\texttt{\\_canon} fix normalises the prefix on both sides, and every life reported here ran after it. Probes run from a clean context (birth prompt only, no brief) for 16 chunks per program with common random seeds derived from seed 777 per (program, chunk), identical for ON and OFF, across checkpoints and across arms.\n\n\\paragraph{Noise bands.} The base model's probe panel is $0.4936 \\pm 0.0113$ over 9 repetitions. We call a pair \\emph{harmful} if \\onoff\\ $< -0.03$, about 2.7 base-panel SD. In the rule game the exam's run-to-run SD was 0.067--0.072 at 8 episodes (means 0.398 and 0.445 on two machines), 0.030--0.044 at 40 episodes (means 0.416, 0.412), and 0.033 at 80 episodes (mean 0.410). The floor did not fall from 40 to 80, so it is generation variance of the same episodes, not sampling; 8-episode exams cannot resolve a $0.03$ tolerance and every classroom result below uses 40. The classroom's harm tolerance of 0.03 is therefore about one SD, and decisions near it flip on nondeterminism: one self-taught lineage rerun with identical configuration on a second machine gave OK/CANARY/OK on one and HARM/HARM/HARM on the other.\n\n\\paragraph{Trainer nondeterminism.} The trainer had no seed flag until we found two default-seed replicates of the same 1,200-row cell differing by 0.059 ($\\approx 5$ base-panel SD); at 12,031 rows same-configuration replicates on two machines differed by 0.078, and two probe panels of one cell differed by 0.147. A seed flag was added; the long lives (v1 writer) remain unseeded. We report cells, not $p$-values.\n\n\\paragraph{Certification bar.} A write recipe is judged on four items: \\emph{absorption} (base NLL minus adapter NLL on the sleep's own rows), \\emph{retention} (the same on earlier sleeps' rows under later adapters), \\emph{interface} (the format canary), and \\emph{no-harm} (paired probes). Transfer beyond the gym's held-out programs is deferred and not claimed. Absorption uses 24 rows per sleep and 24 control rows from an unrelated life; under cumulative training, retention measures ``still trained on'', not resistance to forgetting.\n\n\\paragraph{Contamination rules.} Every CompilerGym life is a disposable development life, never a stage of a child to be raised for confirmation. Bootstrap corpora built from a life that played the gym are quarantined as development-only. A clean child requires a target-blind birth and a fail-closed provenance manifest; no clean child exists yet.\n\n\\paragraph{Arms.} R2: nine ungated, unparented lives (format canary only). R3: probe gate. RP: parental briefs, ungated. R4: gate and parent, launched last and \\emph{in training}. All use the v1 writer.\n\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\n\\subsection{The writer: recipe, rank $\\times$ dose, small-frequent vs one-shot}\n\\label{sec:writer}\n\n\\paragraph{Recipe screen (exploratory).} On a fixed 130-row corpus with two probe panels per cell (v2.1 trainer, 3 epochs, $5\\times10^{-5}$): plain 0.466 (panel spread 0.058); $+$paraphrase 0.496; $+$replay-mix 0.494; both 0.489 (spread 0.002); base $\\approx$ 0.485--0.494. All three enrichments removed the harm and variance of the plain write; none transferred at 130 rows. Paraphrase triples the rows and replay-mix adds $\\max(4,n/5)$ anchors at equal epochs, so dose and diversity are confounded; we froze paraphrase$+$replay-mix pragmatically and do not claim causality.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Rank $\\times$ dose, one-shot v2.1 writes probed on the 8 sealed programs (base $\\approx 0.494$; base-panel SD 0.0113). Values are per-cell probe means; 12,031-row cells have $n=5$ trainer replicates per rank on two machines. Paired $r16-r8$ by (machine, seed): $+0.060, +0.064, -0.015, +0.011, +0.091$.}\n\\label{tab:rankdose}\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nrows & rank 8 & rank 16 \\\\\n\\midrule\n300 & 0.485 (panels 0.477/0.492) & 0.488 (0.491/0.485) \\\\\n1,200 & 0.492, 0.506 (two machines) & 0.456, 0.515 \\\\\n12,031 & 0.413, 0.440, 0.468, 0.491, 0.343 & 0.473, 0.504, 0.453, 0.502, 0.434 \\\\\n & mean 0.431, SD 0.057; below base 5/5 & mean 0.473, SD 0.030; below base 4/5 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Rank $\\times$ dose.} Table~\\ref{tab:rankdose}. At 300 rows the ranks tie. At 1,200 rows the sign of $r16-r8$ flips between two machines ($-0.036$ vs $+0.009$); an earlier reading that ``r16 harms'' was withdrawn: at $\\leq$1,200 rows the rank effect is inside replicate variance. At 12,031 rows (all unique rows pooled across lives) rank 16 beat rank 8 in 4/5 paired replicates (mean $+0.042$, about one pooled SD), and both ranks landed below base: r8 in 5/5 cells, r16 in 4/5. We kept rank 8 (ties go to the smaller rank; roughly 60 GPU-hours were spent on this calibration). The primary finding is \\emph{dose harm}: a one-shot write of the whole pooled corpus makes the agent worse than no adapter.\n\n\\paragraph{Small frequent vs large one-shot.} Lives that wrote every 32 episodes were positive in 69/82 ungated pairs and in every gated pair measured (Section~\\ref{sec:safety}); one-shot writes of 12,031 rows were below base in 9/10 cells. We state this as a difference in \\emph{what corpus is written}, not in optimisation schedule: under cumulative retraining the life's last adapter is itself a one-shot write, but its rows were generated under a sequence of evolving adapters whereas the pooled corpus was not. A planned dose-splitting cell was dropped as degenerate for this reason. The recipes also differ (v1 in lives, v2.1 in the pooled cells), so this is a cell fact across recipes, not a controlled comparison.\n\n\\subsection{Safety: ungated late-life collapse versus gated lives}\n\\label{sec:safety}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Paired \\onoff\\ probes on the 8 sealed programs (harmful $= < -0.03$). R2: nine ungated lives, all 64-episode probes. R3: gated lives at ages 448--640 (latest dated snapshot). RP: parented, ungated. R4 (gate$+$parent): in training, not measured.}\n\\label{tab:safety}\n\\begin{tabular}{llrrrl}\n\\toprule\narm & gating & pairs & positive & harmful & note \\\\\n\\midrule\nR2 (9 lives) & format canary only & 82 & 69 & 9 & harm only after ep.\\ 384, in 3 lives \\\\\nR2, episodes $\\leq 320$ & format canary only & --- & --- & 0 & 0 harmful in 9/9 lives \\\\\nR3 (4 lives) & canary $+$ probe gate & 35 & --- & 0 & means $+0.039/+0.016/+0.055/+0.022$ \\\\\nRP (3 lives) & canary only, parent briefs & 44 & --- & 0 & means $+0.038/+0.016/+0.014$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Ungated (R2).} Table~\\ref{tab:safety} and Appendix~\\ref{app:lives}. Of 82 pairs, 69 were positive, 4 were between $-0.03$ and 0, and 9 were harmful. The harmful pairs came from three lives: one at episodes 384--576 ($-0.038, -0.186, -0.118, -0.039$), one at 448 and 576 ($-0.089, -0.045$; it recovered to about zero by 704--1,024), and one at 640--768 ($-0.039, -0.030, -0.051$). The other six lives were positive at every checkpoint, with mid-life values of $+0.03$ to $+0.065$. Up to episode 320 no life was harmful.\n\n\\paragraph{Two collapse mechanisms (two lives inspected).} First, \\emph{behavioural collapse with perfect format}: the sleep-448 adapter of the worst life produced 1.0--1.8 chunks per episode (act once and stop) against the base's 13, with a parseable-action rate of 1.00; the canary passed at 1.00 and the probe fell $-0.186$. Second, \\emph{a degraded adapter frozen in}: the sleep-608 adapter of another life passed the canary at 0.67 (threshold 0.5) and was harmful; all later candidates failed the canary (0.08, 0.17, 0.00, \\ldots) and were rejected, so the life kept the bad adapter, with 10 rejections against 16 commits. Canary means were also drifting down in two more lives (minima 0.58, means 0.88 and 0.84). The interface item of the certification bar was therefore preserved only as measured by an instrument shown to miss collapse, and the no-harm item failed after about 12 sleeps in 3/9 lives.\n\n\\paragraph{Gated (R3).} The probe gate was proposed as the last mechanism change before a freeze and built the same night. Its first life's gate log: sleep 32, candidate 0.4873 vs floor 0.4847 (base), 11.1 vs 11.6 chunks/episode, DONE; sleep 64, candidate 0.4878 vs 0.4847 with a passing score and perfect format but 2.1 vs 11.6 chunks/episode, REJECTED\\_BREVITY, the collapse shape of Failure~1 caught before commit; sleep 96, candidate 0.4903 vs floor 0.5065 (previous adapter), 7.0 vs 11.1, DONE within the symmetric tolerance, so a slightly worse adapter replaced a better one; sleep 128, 0.5069 vs 0.5065, DONE; sleep 160, 0.4878 vs 0.4878, DONE. That life's paired probes were $+0.042$ at episode 64 and $+0.021$ at 128. Across the four gated lives at ages 448--640: 0 harmful in 35 pairs; life means $+0.039$, $+0.016$, $+0.055$, $+0.022$; rejections 2, 0, 9, 4. The most-rejected life is the best-scoring one. A later undated snapshot lists 5/0/10/4 rejections (including a 0.270 candidate against a 0.527 floor) and still 0 harmful (Appendix~\\ref{app:lives}). No gated life had completed 1,024 episodes at the time of writing; gated lives have passed the age at which ungated harm began (384) but not the age at which it ended (768). We say ``0 harmful so far'', not ``safe''.\n\n\\subsection{Storage is not extraction}\n\\label{sec:storage}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Absorption (base NLL $-$ adapter NLL, nats, response tokens only) for two lives over eight sleeps; 24 rows per sleep, 24 control rows from an unrelated life. Row-specific excess $=$ own rows $-$ control rows.}\n\\label{tab:absorb}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & own rows, sleep 1 $\\to$ 8 & control rows & row-specific excess & retention (sleep-32 rows) \\\\\n\\midrule\nlife A & $3.25 \\to 2.54$ & $1.61 \\to \\sim 1.95$ (plateau by sleep 3) & $1.64 \\to 0.64$ & $3.26$--$3.30$, flat \\\\\nlife B & $3.29 \\to 2.58$ & same plateau & $1.68 \\to 0.64$ & $3.28$--$3.35$, flat \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:absorb}. The adapter makes the agent's own past text roughly $e^{3}\\approx 20$ times likelier, and it does not forget earlier rows under later adapters (as expected when earlier rows remain in every later training set). Over the same lives the paired behaviour change was about $+0.02$ (mean $+0.022$ over the 21 early pairs). The control rows, from a life the adapter never saw, gain about 1.95 nats by the third sleep and then plateau, so most of the stored likelihood is dialect and format; the row-specific part falls from about 1.7 to 0.6 nats across the life, and the base model's own NLL on the child's later text also falls (4.3 to 3.2). Our reading, held loosely: after the format is learned, each sleep adds less that is specific, because the child's later text is more templated (Section~\\ref{sec:parenting}); the write is starved by the loop, not the other way round. We do not claim the adapter stores knowledge the agent can use; it stores text the agent can reproduce.\n\n\\subsection{Parenting: rehearsal, ritual onset, lineages, and what did not separate}\n\\label{sec:parenting}\n\n\\paragraph{Rehearsal.} Under v3 briefs, the fraction of episodes whose first note restated the brief over the last six sleeps was 0.50--0.84, 0.97--1.00 and 0.66--1.00 in the three parented lives. The child does what it is asked, in context, every episode. This is a lexical echo; whether the restated lesson changes the next action, or survives a context reset, is \\nm.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Ritual onset: first 32-episode window with $\\geq 2$ of 4 flags, and persistence. Thresholds were frozen before any parented life reached episode 160.}\n\\label{tab:ritual}\n\\begin{tabular}{llll}\n\\toprule\nlife & episodes & first ritual window & later windows flagged \\\\\n\\midrule\nunparented 0 / 1 / 2 & 424 / 424 / 552 & 192 / 224 / 192 & 7/8, 5/7, 10/12 \\\\\nunparented 3 & 368 & never (two flags never co-occurred) & 0; best scorer, mid-life $+0.065$ \\\\\nunparented 4 / 5 / 6 & 424 / 320 / 320 & 160 / 160 / 160 & 7/9, 6/6, 5/6 \\\\\nolder writer, adult & 864 & 160 & 24/24 from 256 (note overlap 1.00) \\\\\nolder writer, second & 344 & 224 & 4/4 \\\\\n\\midrule\nparented 400 (14B) & 1,024 & 288 & 3/3 \\\\\nparented 401 (14B) & 1,024 & 192; clear 224--320; again from 352 & 7/11 \\\\\nparented 402 (32B-AWQ) & $\\sim$830 & 256; clear 288; again from 320 & 3/4 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Ritual onset is measurable and consistent.} Table~\\ref{tab:ritual}. Onset fell between episodes 160 and 224 (sleeps 5--7) in 8/9 unparented lives with at least 320 episodes; the first-action flag was present from the first window in every life (the birth prompt suggests a recipe, so recipe lock alone is not ritual); once ritual appeared it persisted. The ritual metric was changed mid-study to skip rehearsal notes, so parented windows before and after that fix are not strictly comparable.\n\n\\paragraph{Parented children have not collapsed.} RP~400: 16 pairs, min $+0.006$, max $+0.063$, mean $+0.038$. RP~401: 16 pairs, min $-0.005$, max $+0.025$, mean $+0.016$. RP~402 (32B-AWQ parent, $\\sim$830 episodes): 12 pairs, min $+0.003$, max $+0.025$, mean $+0.014$. Total 44 pairs, 0 harmful, against 3/9 ungated controls harmful after episode 384. At matched ages the parented lives did not separate from controls on paired score. This is a cell fact at $n=3$ vs 9, consistent with ``parenting keeps the write from collapsing'' and not established. The lives were restarted from markers three to four times as the brief prompt changed, and life 402 is incomplete.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Classroom lineages (rule game, three PREV-chained rounds, 40-episode exams, \\onoff\\ per write; band SD 0.030--0.044).
