With a 14B parent, 8/27 writes were clearly positive and 8/27 clearly harmful; self-taught, 4/24 and 11/24. Parented lineage means ranged from $-0.118$ to $+0.101$; self-taught from $-0.079$ to $+0.039$. The direction (fewer harmful, more positive writes with a parent) held through every seed added, and seed-to-seed variance is larger than the arm difference: not established at this $n$. Three things are established at cell level. (a) Single-round writes do not transfer: 1/8 cells positive at 40 episodes, even though the immediate in-context post-minus-pre gain was positive in 5/8. (b) The first write from base is where the parent's advantage concentrated: round-0 parented writes $+0.167, -0.008, +0.008, +0.121, -0.017, +0.100$ (0/6 harmful; the best writes we measured), self-taught round-0 4/6 harmful. (c) Chains degraded under the commit rule as run: the rule compared ON to the base only, and 5 writes were committed below the adapter they replaced (all in parented lineages, by 0.096--0.108); two collapses (ON 0.071 and 0.100) were caught by the harm test. The 0.071 collapse had intact format (parseable-action 0.86) but probed less (5.2 vs 6.3 chunks/episode, 431 vs 728 probes) with shorter chunks (694 vs 870 characters) and failed the quiz: behavioural narrowing, not dialect drift. The proposed fix (also require ON $\\geq$ PREV $- 0.03$) was not applied to keep the series comparable; its analogue for lives became the probe gate. Ritual metrics were computed on each corpus before training.}\n\\label{tab:bootstrap}\n\\begin{tabular}{llrlll}\n\\toprule\ncorpus & source & rows & composition (metaflow/opening/contrast/review/full) & dropped & status \\\\\n\\midrule\nv3 & rule-game classrooms (target-blind) & 470 & 206 / 94 / 70 / 65 / 35 & 7--10 & no flags (recipe share 0.26, note overlap 0.11) \\\\\nv2 & CompilerGym-exposed life & 370 & 152 / 80 / 61 / 52 / 25 & 7--10 & no flags; quarantined, dev-only \\\\\nv1 & same life, lived-heavy control & 552 & --- / 200 / 199 / --- / 153 & 47 & no flags; quarantined, dev-only \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:bootstrap}. The intended first stage of the mechanism sentence is a corpus that installs the habit of reflecting (asking how much more to think, planning, judging a step, reviewing) rather than replaying lived episodes, which would be memorising unlived memories. The structure-heavy mixture (metaflow 0.4, review 0.15, opening 0.2, contrast 0.15, full 0.1) yields 470 target-blind rows with no ritual flags. No bootstrap adapter has been trained or measured; the queued adapters are \\emph{in training}, and the target-blind corpus is not yet certified as a clean birth because its upstream ledgers have not passed a fail-closed provenance guard. Every bootstrap effect is \\nm.\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep as a frequency amplifier (reading, held loosely).} Four measurements point the same way. The adapter reproduces its own rows strongly ($\\sim$3 nats) and moves behaviour little ($\\sim$$+0.02$). When the corpus contains something different, behaviour moves a lot: a first parented classroom write moved the exam by $+0.10$ to $+0.17$, and a pooled 12k-row one-shot moved it far in the wrong direction; so the base is receptive and rank is not the bottleneck (r8 $\\approx$ r16). Retention is flat, so nothing is forgotten; late in life each sleep writes back the child's most frequent recent behaviour, and the cumulative corpus is dominated by old habit rows. Lessons work in context (immediate gains in 5/8 classroom sets; one four-window remission) and vanish within about two sleeps, because the child's own thoughts still mostly contain the old template. The reading: the child is receptive and the sleep amplifies whatever is frequent. A lesson survives a sleep only if it has become the child's own frequent behaviour before the write, or if the compiler stops amplifying repeats. Falsifiers: under repetition briefs, rehearsal rows should appear in the ledger within one to two sleeps and ritual windows should become rarer than controls over the following four or more (the first part held, the second did not yet); and a compiler that collapses near-duplicate rows should lower the late-life harm rate. Neither the dedup lever nor a ritual-aware gate is built.\n\n\\paragraph{Why repetition.} If sleep amplifies frequency, the only way a context-side lesson reaches the weights is by becoming frequent in the child's own text first. Hence v3: the parent repeats one lesson and asks the child to restate it before acting, every episode. The rehearsal rates (0.50--1.00) show the child complies; they do not show uptake, and literal repetition could itself become a ritual, which is why rehearsal notes are excluded from the ritual metric and why uptake would need to be measured as unprompted, differently worded, situation-selective use that changes the next action and survives a context reset.\n\n\\paragraph{Why the thinker/compiler line.} The parent's words could have been added to the corpus and the child fine-tuned on them; that is post-training, and it would remove the thing under study, which is whether a child can be taught to think in a way that its own sleep then preserves. Keeping the compiler organisational (select, canonicalise, de-duplicate, interleave) also keeps the write inspectable: every row is text the child produced in a context we stored.\n\n\\paragraph{The target: state-to-state reasoning.} The base model already reasons token to token and can change its mind in context. What we want the loop to train is reasoning from one state to the next: plan, execute to a self-chosen end, review (how did I judge this, where did I go wrong, what generalises), and carry the review into the next state's plan. The PLAN/EXECUTE/REVIEW structure is already the rendering target of the bootstrap corpora; it is not yet the live stream. A stream without a terminal marker, state boundaries as harness events, and branch-and-join thinking under a learned budget are the planned next mechanism changes, not part of the reported system.\n\n\\paragraph{What a 7-day child would need.} Nothing here is about a 7-day child. To get there, the record says: a writer that passes the certification bar with a score gate at every sleep, a behavioural canary, a paired format canary, and a recovery path after repeated rejections (only the first two are built); a clean, target-blind birth with a fail-closed manifest; and a comparison against a matched agent with the same tools and frozen weights. The 1,024-episode lives are a floor, not a ceiling; a short-horizon null should be read as ``not yet'' unless the learning-versus-lifetime curve says otherwise.\n\n\\paragraph{Limitations.} One gym with about 67 training programs replayed; 8 held-out programs; one base model; one adapter rank in lives. Nine ungated, four gated, and three parented lives; two lives for absorption; 9 vs 8 classroom lineages. All long-life results come from the bare-text v1 writer and characterise that writer; they do not certify the response-masked v2.1 writer, and switching a life's writer is a new lineage. The trainer was unseeded in lives, and same-configuration replicates differ by up to 0.078. Three lives were interrupted once by an operator error and resumed from the last committed sleep boundary. Gate thresholds (0.02, 0.5) and ritual thresholds (0.7/0.05/0.5/0.7, two flags) are written-down definitions, not calibrated instruments, and the gate's symmetric tolerance let a 0.4903 candidate replace a 0.5065 adapter. The probe gate has not yet been independently ratified. None of the closest external baselines (a QA-extraction LoRA writer, a learned textual-memory updater, a batch reflective-distillation control) has been run against this system: all \\nm.\n\n\\section{Related work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{The axis.} Recurrence in activations is the looped or depth-recurrent transformer \\cite{TODO-looped-transformers}; recurrence in tokens is chain-of-thought and its verbal-feedback descendants: Reflexion keeps lessons as text in an episodic buffer without weight updates \\cite{shinn2023reflexion}, Generative Agents synthesise reflections over a memory stream \\cite{park2023generativeagents}, ExpeL extracts insights ``without requiring parametric updates'' \\cite{zhao2023expel}, and Voyager keeps a skill library with frozen weights \\cite{wang2023voyager}. Our NOTE/RECALL is the same move at wake; SLEEP is the added step. The transformer removed recurrence to buy training parallelism; looped models put it back inside the forward pass and pay at inference; we put it back at consolidation time, where serialisation does not bind, and agent-level recurrence adds new information per cycle as well as compute.\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep consolidation.} Complementary learning systems justify a fast episodic store and slow interleaved consolidation \\cite{mcclelland1995cls}; active system consolidation licenses repeated small cycles rather than one batch \\cite{diekelmann2010sleep}; synaptic homeostasis says sleep keeps what is consistently reused \\cite{tononi2014shy}, which is the neuroscience analogue of our amplifier reading; replay is biased and mixes new with old \\cite{buzsaki2015swr}; targeted reactivation shows selection is steerable from outside \\cite{oudiette2013tmr}, the nearest analogue of parenting; and consolidation must be regulated, not exhaustive \\cite{sun2023organizing}, consistent with our dose harm. In machine learning, wake-sleep trains on self-generated data \\cite{hinton1995wakesleep}; generative replay interleaves old with new \\cite{shin2017generativereplay}; CLS-ER consolidates continuously without a sleep stage \\cite{arani2022clser}. Offline recurrence into fast weights \\cite{lee2026lmsleep} and a ``Sleep'' training paradigm with consolidation and dreaming \\cite{behrouz2026lmneedsleep} are the closest sleep-framed neighbours; neither writes a single agent's lived, gated continuations.\n\n\\paragraph{Knowledge extractability.} A fact seen once in one form is stored but not extractable; multiple renderings at training time make it retrievable \\cite{allenzhu2023physics}. Our absorption--behaviour gap is that result in our units, and the recipe screen (plain 0.466 vs enriched 0.489--0.496) is the augmentation condition, confounded with dose. System-2 fine-tuning reaches the same conclusion with self-generated paraphrases and QA \\cite{park2025newnews}; LoRA has been studied directly as a knowledge memory \\cite{back2026loraknowledge}.\n\n\\paragraph{Parametric and textual memory for agents.} Online LoRA fast weights with QA self-supervision \\cite{ren2026tmem}, per-category adapters written from failure--correction pairs in Minecraft \\cite{guo2026peam}, surprise-gated LoRA consolidation \\cite{TODO-evaf}, reflective distillation into weights \\cite{TODO-leafe}, early-experience supervision \\cite{TODO-early-experience}, and learned textual-memory updaters \\cite{TODO-memopilot,TODO-spark} all precede us: language agents that learn from their own outcomes, carry online LoRA state, or consolidate selectively are occupied claims. What remains ours is one acting policy accumulating an individual life through repeated gated writes of its own text, and the failure characterisation above. Dreamer's ``imagination'' \\cite{hafner2023dreamerv3} and DECKARD's dream/wake phases \\cite{nottingham2023deckard} are world-model senses of the word; our DREAM is context management. Continual learning is the contrast, not the frame: modular memory positions \\cite{dorovatas2026modularmemory} and the finding that external memory relocates rather than removes the stability--plasticity problem \\cite{hu2026clmemory} both raise the bar for measuring an adapter's own interference. Zahavy's argument that language models lack abduction \\cite{zahavy2026cantjump} is motivation: the ingredients he asks for (internal simulation, strong learned priors, first-class hypothesis generation) are what the loop is meant to train, where checkable evidence exists.\n\n\\section*{Reproducibility statement}\nAll numbers in this paper are cell counts or measured means taken from logged runs; each is traceable to a dated laboratory-notebook entry or the compiled evidence table, and the mapping is released with the code. We release the harness (life loop, probes, gates), both writers, the compiler, the ritual detector, the parent backend with leak scan, the classroom round, the bootstrap renderer, and the absorption probe, plus the birth and parent prompts (Appendix~\\ref{app:prompts}) and every gate and metric threshold (Appendices~\\ref{app:gates}--\\ref{app:ritual}). The probe split is sealed by name after identifier normalisation. Raw probe and gate JSON for every life is released with per-life provenance; hardware and scheduling details appear generically in Appendix~\\ref{app:infra}. Known nondeterminism (unseeded v1 trainer; same-configuration gaps up to 0.078) is reported rather than averaged away.\n\n\\section*{AI-use statement}\nCode, experiment orchestration, log analysis, and the drafting of this manuscript were assisted by two AI systems (Claude and Codex), including the construction of measurement instruments and the auditing of claims against the run logs. All numbers come from logged runs; no result was generated or estimated by a language model. The parent and author models described in the paper are components of the studied system, not authors. The human authors designed the study, made every design ruling reported here, and are responsible for all claims.\n\n\\bibliography{refs}\n\\bibliographystyle{iclr2027_conference}\n\n\\appendix\n\\section{Prompts}\n\\label{app:prompts}\n\n\\paragraph{Birth prompt (identical in both arms).} The only hand-written artefact. It defines the five markers (\\texttt{PREDICT: <number>}, \\texttt{ACT: <passes>}, \\texttt{NOTE: <text>}, \\texttt{RECALL: <query>}, \\texttt{DONE}), tells the agent to mind the clock, to investigate surprises, to judge itself, and that it is measured on programs it has never seen. It contains an example action (a four-pass opening), which caps what ``discovery'' can mean: the recipe that later ritualises is the one the prompt suggests. \\todo{paste verbatim text of the birth prompt file here.}\n\n\\paragraph{Episode texts (gym).} Goal: ``Optimize program `$\\langle$id$\\rangle$': choose LLVM optimization passes that minimize its IR instruction count.'' Metric: ``score = (base\\_instructions $-$ after) / base. Higher is better; 0 = no improvement. Passes are applied in the order you give them.'' Intro: ``New program: $\\langle$id$\\rangle$. I should form an expectation before acting, and write down what I learn.''\n\n\\paragraph{Parent prompt.} Ten teaching principles: predict before acting; surprises are gold; cheap experiments first; scope your memories (one case is an anecdote, two a candidate pattern, claims carry their evidence count); build up then build down; diversity before commitment; mind the clock; notes are your future mind; recall before re-deriving; judge yourself. Conversational rules: Socratic when the child is close, direct when far; ask for restatement and application; praise specifics; critique notes for scope. Hard rules: never give answers, never name compiler passes, never reveal scores; under 200 words per message. \\todo{paste verbatim parent prompt file.}\n\n\\paragraph{Correction call (classroom).} The parent sees its playbook (first 3,000 characters), optionally ``[DIAGNOSTIC ONLY --- NEVER STATE THIS] the hidden answer is: \\ldots'', the last 4,000 characters of the child's transcript, and: ``Name the ONE most important PROCESS mistake (never the answer), under 100 words, then ask the child to restate the lesson.'' Generation: 220 tokens, temperature 0.4.\n\n\\paragraph{Leak scan and fallback.} Patterns: \\emph{the rule is}, \\emph{the answer is}, \\emph{divisible by}, \\emph{strictly increasing}, \\emph{contains a zero}, \\emph{all even}, \\emph{product is even}, \\emph{first is the largest}, \\emph{sum (is) greater than}, \\emph{at least two equal}, \\emph{spread at most}, \\emph{middle is the average}; a pass-name pattern (\\texttt{-mem2reg|-sroa|-gvn|-simplifycfg|-instcombine|-licm}); the hidden rule by exact substring or by at least half of its content words as whole words (added after exact matching missed paraphrases such as ``all numbers must be even''). Fallback text: ``I noticed something in your process worth examining. Before your next probe, state exactly which of your hypotheses it would distinguish, and what result you expect from each.'' Since the third brief version, a pattern hit whose matched text already appears verbatim in the child's own sampled thinking is not treated as a leak (the parent quoting the child's ritual recipe back), because the pass-name pattern had blocked 4/16 and 6/14 briefs in two lives.\n\n\\paragraph{Brief prompts.} \\emph{v1} (generic): asked for a $\\leq 8$-line process-only brief when the child's thinking was ritualised. First delivered brief head: ``It looks like you've fallen into a routine with your predictions and actions\\ldots Predict: Each time, vary your expected outcomes\\ldots''. Reason changed: the prediction advice was wrong; varying predictions for variety destroys the prediction-to-surprise signal. \\emph{v2}: PREDICT must be a consequence of a named feature of this situation, with a reason and a range (the same prediction is fine when situations are alike, but say why); NOTE must contain a contrast with a specific earlier case, what differed, and a scope; RECALL must be a specific similar-situation query; when the first action has repeated for many episodes, run one deliberate deviation per episode and predict its effect first; process only, never name actions. Reason changed: flags cleared briefly and ritual returned in all three parented lives. \\emph{v3} (repetition): the parent sees its previous brief ($\\leq 1{,}200$ characters) and the child's rehearsal rate and is told ``Keep the SAME core lesson --- repetition is how it will take. Do not switch to a new lesson; sharpen the same one, acknowledge what the child has started doing, and insist on the rest.'' Every brief ends: ``Repeat after me, every episode, in your own words, as your first NOTE before you act: what the ritual was and what you do instead. Keep repeating it until it is simply how you think.'' The latest brief is shown at every wake. Brief generation: 320 tokens, temperature 0.4; brief truncated to 1,900 characters.\n\n\\section{Gate definitions and thresholds}\n\\label{app:gates}\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\textbf{Canonicalisation.} Before any row enters a corpus, marker lines matching \\verb|^\\s*(#{1,6}\\s*|[-*]\\s+|\\*\\*|>\\s*)+\\s*(PREDICT|ACT|NOTE|RECALL|DONE)| are rewritten to ``MARKER: ''. Reason: the base emits decorated markers in $\\sim$30\\% of chunks and a first corpus that captures them locks the dialect in for life.\n\\item \\textbf{Format canary (lives).} Candidate adapter runs the first 4 probe programs for 3 chunks each in the real gym context (seeds 4242$+i$); pass rate $=$ fraction of raw chunks matching \\verb|^ACT:\\s*\\S|; pass iff rate $\\geq 0.5$. Reason: a synthetic-prompt canary passed while the adapter emitted only decorated markers in gym context. Known limit: passed at 1.00 during a behavioural collapse and at 0.67 for a harmful adapter.\n\\item \\textbf{Paired canary (classrooms).} ON parseable-action rate $\\geq$ OFF rate $- 0.10$, measured over ledger thought rows only. Reason: the base's own rate in the rule-game exam context ranged 0.19--0.95, and an earlier denominator that included intro and outcome lines recorded 0.21 where the true rate was 0.93, producing two false rejections in the smoke test.\n\\item \\textbf{Probe gate (score).} Candidate mean on the seeded 8-program mini-probe $\\geq \\max(\\text{latest base OFF probe},\\ \\text{latest adapter ON probe}) - 0.02$; at sleep 32 the floor is the base probe at episode 0. Tolerance $0.02 \\approx 2$ base-panel SD. Known limit: the tolerance is symmetric, so a candidate up to 0.02 below the previous adapter replaces it (observed: 0.4903 replaced 0.5065). An open question is whether replacing PREV should need a tighter margin (e.g.\\ $0.01$).\n\\item \\textbf{Probe gate (brevity / behavioural canary).} Candidate chunks per episode on the mini-probe $\\geq 0.5 \\times$ base chunks per episode (chunks $=$ thought rows / 8). Reason: collapsed adapters act once and stop (1--2 chunks vs 11--13).\n\\item \\textbf{Verdicts.} DONE, REJECTED\\_CANARY, REJECTED\\_SCORE, REJECTED\\_BREVITY. Only DONE adapters are loaded; a rejected sleep leaves the previous adapter in place. A recovery path after repeated rejections (re-fork from the last adapter that passed the score gate with a smaller-lr write) is proposed and not built.\n\\item \\textbf{Classroom commit rule (as run).} Commit iff paired canary passes and ON $\\geq$ OFF $- 0.03$. PREV was recorded and not used; 5 writes were committed below the adapter they replaced. Proposed fix (not applied to the reported series): also require ON $\\geq$ PREV $- 0.03$.\n\\item \\textbf{World admission (classroom).} A lesson is admitted iff the child's best score on the apply task $\\geq$ its best score on the pre task; only rows from admitted pairs enter the corpus. Strata minimum shares: dialect anchor 0.10, prediction revision 0.15, evidence scope 0.10, stopping 0.05, memory use 0.05, old experience 0.15, new experience 0.40; exact target 400 rows without duplication; shortfall reported, never padded.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\section{Ritual and rehearsal metrics}\n\\label{app:ritual}\nThought rows are grouped into episode \\emph{instances}: a new instance of a program starts whenever its chunk index does not increase (wake batches interleave programs, and grouping by program identifier alone made a 424-episode life look like 67 episodes; fixed before any brief fired). Over the last 32 instances (at least 4 required):\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\textbf{same\\_recipe}: share of instances whose first \\texttt{ACT} payload (whitespace removed) equals the modal one, $\\geq 0.7$;\n\\item \\textbf{flat\\_predictions}: population SD of parsed \\texttt{PREDICT} values $< 0.05$, with at least 8 predictions;\n\\item \\textbf{templated\\_notes}: mean Jaccard similarity of content-token sets (\\verb|[a-z]{3,}|) between consecutive instances' first \\texttt{NOTE}s $\\geq 0.5$; since the third brief version, first notes that restate the brief (share $\\geq 4$ content words with it) are dropped before this is computed;\n\\item \\textbf{same\\_recall}: share of \\texttt{RECALL} queries equal to the modal one $\\geq 0.7$, with at least 8 recalls.\n\\end{itemize}\n\\textbf{Ritual} $=$ at least two flags. Thresholds were written down and frozen before any parented life crossed episode 160; a synthetic templated ledger raises all four flags and a varied one raises none. \\textbf{Rehearsal rate} $=$ fraction of the last 32 instances with a note whose first note shares $\\geq 4$ content tokens with the most recent brief. It is an echo diagnostic.\n\n\\section{Per-life tables}\n\\label{app:lives}\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Ungated fixed-writer lives (R2; v1 writer; format canary only). ``Resumed'' lives were interrupted once by an operator error and continued from the last committed sleep with the same seeded episode order.}\n\\begin{tabular}{lp{4.2cm}p{4.2cm}p{3.6cm}}\n\\toprule\nlife & early paired \\onoff\\ (ep.\\ 64$\\to$) & harmful pairs (episode) & notes \\\\\n\\midrule\n0 & $+0.019, +0.013, +0.011, +0.015$ & none & every pair positive; canary min 0.58 / mean 0.88; resumed \\\\\n1 & $+0.003, +0.007, +0.050, +0.048$ & none & every pair positive; resumed \\\\\n2 & $+0.044, +0.006, +0.018, +0.003, +0.024$ & $-0.039, -0.030, -0.051$ (640--768) & sleep-608 adapter passed canary at 0.67; 10 later rejections, 16 commits; frozen on bad adapter \\\\\n3 & $+0.018, +0.051, +0.045$ & none & mid-life $+0.065$; never sustained ritual \\\\\n4 & $+0.009, +0.030, +0.021$ & none & canary min 0.58 / mean 0.84 \\\\\n5 & $+0.025, +0.010$ & $-0.038, -0.186, -0.118, -0.039$ (384--576) & sleep 448: 1.0--1.8 chunks/episode, parseable-action 1.00; resumed \\\\\n6 & --- & $-0.089, -0.045$ (448, 576) & recovered to $\\sim 0$ by 704--1,024 \\\\\n7, 8 & --- & none & every pair positive; youngest lives \\\\\n\\midrule\ntotal & & 9/82 harmful; 69/82 positive; 4/82 in $[-0.03, 0]$ & 0 harmful at episodes $\\leq 320$ in 9/9 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Gated lives (R3; v1 writer; canary $+$ probe gate). Lives 400 and 402 were not flagged at 160 or 192.\n\n\\section{Classroom lineage table}\n\\label{app:lineages}\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\\small\n\\caption{Every write in the classroom series (rule game; three PREV-chained rounds; 40-episode exams; \\onoff\\ per write; band SD 0.030--0.044; ``rej'' $=$ rejected by the harm or canary test and not committed). ``m1/m2'' $=$ the two independent machines; same seed on both machines is a same-configuration replicate.}\n\\begin{tabular}{llrrrr}\n\\toprule\narm & lineage & round 0 & round 1 & round 2 & mean \\\\\n\\midrule\n14B & s8000 m2 & $+0.167$ & $+0.008$ & $-0.312$ rej & $-0.046$ \\\\\n14B & s8001 m2 & $-0.008$ & $+0.012$ & $-0.012$ & $-0.003$ \\\\\n14B & s8000 m1 & $+0.008$ & $-0.012$ & $+0.037$ & $+0.011$ \\\\\n14B & s8001 m1 & $+0.121$ & $+0.096$ & $+0.017$ & $+0.078$ \\\\\n14B & s8002 m2 & $-0.017$ & $-0.029$ & $-0.113$ rej & $-0.053$ \\\\\n14B & s8003 m2 & $+0.100$ & $0.000$ & $-0.100$ rej & $0.000$ \\\\\n14B & s8004 m2 & $+0.100$ & $+0.054$ & $+0.150$ & $+0.101$ \\\\\n14B & s8005 m2 & $-0.138$ rej & $-0.150$ rej & $-0.067$ rej & $-0.118$ \\\\\n14B & s8005 m1 & $-0.104$ rej & $+0.017$ & $-0.238$ rej & $-0.108$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nself & s8000 m2 & $-0.025$ & $-0.013$ rej (canary) & $+0.008$ & $-0.010$ \\\\\nself & s8001 m2 & $-0.133$ rej & $-0.008$ & $+0.037$ & $-0.035$ \\\\\nself & s8000 m1 & $-0.075$ rej & $-0.096$ rej & $-0.067$ rej & $-0.079$ \\\\\nself & s8002 m2 & $-0.096$ rej & $-0.071$ rej & $-0.008$ & $-0.058$ \\\\\nself & s8003 m2 & $+0.029$ & $+0.071$ & $-0.033$ rej & $+0.022$ \\\\\nself & s8001 m1 & $-0.075$ rej & $-0.008$ & $-0.067$ rej & $-0.050$ \\\\\nself & s8004 m1 & $+0.129$ & $+0.021$ & $-0.033$ rej & $+0.039$ \\\\\nself & s8005 m2 & $-0.083$ rej & $+0.083$ & $+0.017$ & $+0.006$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{By round.} Parented: round 0 harmful 0/6 (3/6 above $+0.09$), round 1 0/6, round 2 3/6. Self-taught: round 0 4/6, round 1 2/6, round 2 3/6 (six lineages per arm at the time of that tally). Every degraded parented third write came from a child playing under an adapter committed below PREV or at zero gain.\n\n\\paragraph{Below-PREV commits (all parented).} s8000 m2 round 1 (0.104 below PREV 0.442); s8001 m2 round 2 (0.108 below 0.450); s8000 m1 rounds 1 and 2; s8003 m2 round 1 (0.096 below 0.463). Collapses caught by the harm test: ON 0.071 (s8000 m2 round 2) and ON 0.100 (s8005 m1 round 2).\n\n\\paragraph{Best single write.} s8000 m2 round 0: ON 0.508 / OFF 0.342 $= +0.167$; 19/32 lessons admitted; canary ON/OFF 0.97/0.88. The OFF exam (0.342) was below the 40-episode band means ($\\sim$0.41--0.45).\n\n\\paragraph{Leak blocks per lineage (utterances replaced by fallback, of 96).} 14B: 12, 6, 4, 10, 7 across five lineages. Parent-size cell (seed 9000, $n=1$): 32B-AWQ 21/96, 14B 6/96. That cell's writes: 32B-AWQ $-0.087$ rej, $-0.029$, $-0.054$ rej; 14B $+0.013$, $-0.167$ rej, $+0.075$; self $0.000$, $-0.117$ rej, $-0.100$ rej.\n\n\\paragraph{Single-round cells (40 episodes, seeds 7004--7007).} 14B: $-0.012, -0.058, +0.058, -0.167$ (mean $-0.045$); self: $-0.138, -0.042, -0.050, -0.021$ (mean $-0.063$). 1/8 positive; immediate in-context post$-$pre positive in 5/8. Earlier 8-episode scouts ($n=4$ pairs) are underpowered and are not evidence.\n\n\\paragraph{Provenance flag.} One parented lineage (s8000 m2) failed at round 1 when its playbook prompt exceeded the parent server's context, resumed at the round-1 sleep, and skipped its round-1 playbook rewrite; playbook input was then bounded to $\\leq 40$ admission rows $+ \\leq 20$ other rows, $\\leq 9{,}000$ characters.\n\n\\section{Corpus compositions and sleep-corpus facts}\n\\label{app:corpora}\n\\paragraph{Bootstrap corpora.} Table~\\ref{tab:bootstrap}. Renderings: METAFLOW (10--16 lines of first-person self-questioning over the real context before any action, ending in one NOTE with plan and stopping rule); REVIEW (one 6--10 line NOTE judging the thinking); OPENING (next-episode opening: RECALL, NOTE restating the review and plan, PREDICT with reason and range); CONTRAST (5--8 line NOTE contrasting with a named earlier program); FULL (the whole episode restructured, action set a subset of the original). Non-FULL renderings must contain no ACT line. Default mixture 0.4/0.15/0.2/0.15/0.1; v1 $=$ full, opening, contrast each with probability 1. Author: 32B-AWQ. Ritual metrics per corpus treat each rendering as one pseudo-episode.\n\n\\paragraph{Sleep corpora across a life (ambiguous, not an outcome).} New rows per sleep fall about $4\\times$ across a life (e.g.\\ 127 $\\to$ 30; 134 $\\to$ 33; 115 $\\to$ 5--35) while characters per row rise about $3\\times$ (314 $\\to$ 791; 308 $\\to$ 949; 310 $\\to$ 815). This could be abstraction, ritualised admission collapse, or verbosity; we do not claim compression.\n\n\\paragraph{Rank-calibration corpus.} 12,031 unique rows pooled from all lives; a large cell took about 4 hours to train plus 25 minutes to probe on one GPU.\n\n\\section{Infrastructure notes (no identifiers)}\n\\label{app:infra}\nChild and parents were served with vLLM on 48\\,GB GPUs across two independent machines; the child engine used a 16,384-token window, temperature 0.7, and 400-token chunks. A 32B parent in bf16 with tensor parallelism across two GPUs hung three times (once at collective initialisation, twice at a shared-memory broadcast wait) and was abandoned in favour of a 4-bit AWQ model on one GPU. Lives are idempotent and resumable through marker files at every phase; three lives were resumed once after an operator mistake killed every engine process on one machine. The probe gate adds one 8-episode probe per sleep ($\\sim$6 minutes). Rank calibration cost about 60 GPU-hours. The same-configuration cross-machine gaps reported in the main text (0.059, 0.078; OK-vs-HARM flips) are hardware and checkpointing nondeterminism under an unseeded trainer; a seed flag has since been added to the v2.1 trainer. Everything reported as ``in training'' (gate$+$parent lives, bootstrap adapters) was running at submission and has no measured outcome.\n\n\\end{document}",
